This document provides a comprehensive reference for JDBC formulas supported in DataGOL. These formulas enable powerful data processing, analysis, and transformation capabilities directly within your DataGOL workflows.

Data aggregation: Calculate sums, averages, counts, and statistical measures Text processing: Clean, format, and manipulate string data Date/Time operations: Parse, format, and calculate with dates and timestamps Conditional logic: Implement business rules and data validation Mathematical operations: Perform calculations and statistical analysis

Purpose:​ Removes negative signs from numbers. Usage:​ ABS(number) Example:​ returns 25 ABS(-25) Use Case:​ Calculating distances, finding differences without caring about direction, cleaning up negative values in reports.

Purpose:​ Always rounds numbers up to the next whole number. Usage:​ CEIL(number) Example:​ Returns 5 CEIL(4.1) Use Case:​ Used for calculating minimum packages needed, determining required resources, and inventory planning.

Purpose:​ Always rounds numbers down to the previous whole number. Usage:​ FLOOR(number) Example:​ Returns 4 FLOOR(4.9) Use Case:​ Useful for calculating completed units, determining available capacity, and budget calculations.

Purpose:​ Rounds numbers to the nearest whole number or specified decimal places. Usage:​ ROUND(number, decimal_places) Example:​ Returns 123.46 ROUND(123.456, 2) Use Case:​ Applied in financial calculations, displaying prices, and creating clean reports.

Purpose:​ Multiplies a number by itself a specified number of times. Usage:​ POWER(base, exponent) Example:​ Returns 8 (2×2×2) POWER(2, 3) Use Case:​ Used for compound interest calculations, growth projections, and area/volume calculations.

Purpose:​ Finds what number multiplied by itself equals the given number. Usage:​ SQRT(number) Example:​ Returns 4 SQRT(16) Use Case:​ Applied in statistical calculations, geometric measurements, and risk analysis.

Purpose:​ Mathematical function for advanced calculations and modeling. Usage:​ LN(number) Example:​ Returns 2.302585 LN(10) Use Case:​ Used in scientific calculations, decay models, and financial modeling.
Purpose:​ Returns the mathematical constant $\pi$ (3.14159...). Usage:​ PI() Example:​ Returns 3.14159 PI() Use Case:​ Used in circle calculations, geometric formulas, and engineering calculations.

Purpose:​ Shows what's left over after division. Usage:​ MOD(dividend, divisor) Example:​ Returns 1 (10÷3 = 3 remainder 1) MOD(10, 3) Use Case:​ Useful for creating alternating patterns, pagination, and scheduling rotations.

Purpose:​ Calculates the mean value of a group of numbers. Usage:​ AVG(column_name) Example:​ Might return 50000 AVG(salary) Use Case:​ Used for performance metrics, salary analysis, quality scores, and customer ratings.

Purpose:​ Adds up all numbers in a group. Usage:​ SUM(column_name) Example:​ Might return 125000 SUM(sales) Use Case:​ Used for revenue totals, expense calculations, inventory counts, and performance totals.

Purpose:​ Counts how many items exist (ignores empty values). Usage:​ COUNT(column_name) Example:​ Might return 150 COUNT(customer_id) Use Case:​ Used for customer counts, order quantities, active users, and completion rates.
Purpose:​ Finds the lowest number in a group. Usage:​ MIN(column_name) Example:​ Might return 9.99 MIN(price) Use Case:​ Used for lowest prices, minimum scores, earliest dates, and budget floors.
Purpose:​ Finds the highest number in a group. Usage:​ MAX(column_name) Example:​ Might return 98 MAX(score) Use Case:​ Used for peak performance, highest prices, latest dates, and record highs.

Purpose:​ Finds the middle number when all values are arranged in order. Usage:​ MEDIAN(column_name) Example:​ Might return 45000 MEDIAN(income) Use Case:​ Used for salary benchmarks, performance baselines, and market analysis.

Purpose:​ Measures how spread out numbers are from the average. Usage:​ STDDEV(column_name) Example:​ Might return 2.5 STDDEV(response_time) Use Case:​ Used for quality control, performance consistency, and risk assessment.

Purpose:​ Measures how much numbers vary from the average (squared differences). Usage:​ VARIANCE(column_name) Example:​ Might return 1250000 VARIANCE(sales) Use Case:​ Used for financial analysis, quality metrics, and forecasting accuracy.

Purpose:​ Combines multiple pieces of text into one. Usage:​ CONCAT(text1, text2, text3...) Example:​ Returns "Hello World" CONCAT('Hello', ' ', 'World') Use Case:​ Used for creating full names, building addresses, generating reports, and email formatting.

Purpose:​ Converts all letters to capital letters. Usage:​ UPPER(text) Example:​ Returns "HELLO" UPPER('hello') Use Case:​ Used for standardizing data entry, creating consistent formats, and report headers.
Purpose:​ Converts all letters to small letters. Usage:​ LOWER(text) Example:​ Returns "hello" LOWER('HELLO') Use Case:​ Used for email addresses, usernames, data cleaning, and search functions.

Purpose:​ Makes the first letter of each word uppercase. Usage:​ INITCAP(text) Example:​ Returns "John Smith" INITCAP('john smith') Use Case:​ Used for proper names, titles, address formatting, and professional correspondence.

Purpose:​ Removes spaces from the beginning and end of text. Usage:​ TRIM(text) Example:​ Returns "Hello World" TRIM(' Hello World ') Use Case:​ Used for data cleaning, form processing, and import/export cleanup.
Purpose:​ Removes spaces only from the beginning of the text. Usage:​ LTRIM(text) Example:​ Returns "Hello" LTRIM(' Hello') Use Case:​ Used for data formatting, code cleanup, and text alignment.

Purpose:​ Takes out a specific part of the text. Usage:​ SUBSTRING(text, start_position, length) Example:​ Returns "atab" SUBSTRING('Database', 2, 4) Use Case:​ Used for extracting codes, parsing data, creating abbreviations, and ID processing.

Purpose:​ Takes a specified number of characters from the end of the text. Usage:​ RIGHT(text, number_of_characters) Example:​ Returns "base" RIGHT('Database', 4) Use Case:​ Used for file extensions, postal codes, ID suffixes, and validation codes.

Purpose:​ Finds and replaces text patterns using advanced matching rules. Usage:​ REGEXP_REPLACE(text, pattern, replacement, flags) Example:​ Returns 1234567890 REGEXP_REPLACE('123-456-7890', '-', '', 'g') Use Case:​ Used for phone number formatting, data cleaning, removing special characters, and standardizing formats.
Purpose:​ Returns today's date. Usage:​ CURRENT_DATE Example:​ Returns 2025-01-22 CURRENT_DATE Use Case:​ Used for timestamping records, calculating ages, due date calculations, and report dating.

Purpose:​ Returns the exact current date and time. Usage:​ CURRENT_TIMESTAMP Example:​ Returns 2025-01-22 10:15:30 CURRENT_TIMESTAMP Use Case:​ Used for transaction logging, audit trails, real-time reporting, and activity tracking.

Purpose:​ Calculates the number of days between two dates. Usage:​ AGE(end_date, start_date) Example:​ Returns 7 AGE('2025-01-22', '2025-01-15') Use Case:​ Used for customer tenure, project duration, payment delays, and service periods.

Purpose:​ Pulls out specific parts of a date (year, month, day, etc.). Usage:​ DATE_PART('part', date) Example:​ Returns 2025 DATE_PART('year', '2025-01-22') Use Case:​ Used for monthly reports, yearly summaries, seasonal analysis, and age calculations.

Purpose:​ Rounds dates down to a specific time period. Usage:​ DATE_TRUNC('precision', date) Example:​ Returns 2025-01-01 DATE_TRUNC('month', '2025-01-22') Use Case:​ Used for monthly grouping, quarterly reports, trend analysis, and data aggregation.

Purpose:​ Returns the first non-empty value from a list. Usage:​ COALESCE(value1, value2, value3...) Example:​ Returns "Fallback" COALESCE(NULL, 'Fallback', 'Default') Use Case:​ Used for default values, handling missing data, report formatting, and data validation.

Purpose:​ Creates an if-then-else logic for different scenarios. Usage:​ CASE WHEN condition1 THEN result1 WHEN condition2 THEN result2 ELSE default_result END Example:​ Assigns 'A' if score >= 90, 'B' if score >= 80, else 'C' CASE WHEN score >= 90 THEN 'A' WHEN score >= 80 THEN 'B' ELSE 'C' END Use Case:​ Used for grade calculations, status assignments, categorization, conditional formatting, and business rules.

Column and table names​ -- ✅ GOOD: Clear, descriptive names SELECT customer_first_name, order_total_amount FROM customer_orders -- ❌ AVOID: Cryptic abbreviations SELECT cust_fn, ord_tot_amt FROM cust_ord Formula aliases​ -- ✅ GOOD: Meaningful aliases SELECT CONCAT(first_name, ' ', last_name) AS full_name, AVG(salary) AS average_salary, COUNT(*) AS total_employees -- ❌ AVOID: Generic or no aliases SELECT CONCAT(first_name, ' ', last_name), AVG(salary) AS avg1, COUNT(*) AS cnt

Readable structure​ -- ✅ GOOD: Well-formatted and indented SELECT department_name, COUNT(employee_id) AS employee_count, AVG(salary) AS average_salary, MAX(hire_date) AS latest_hire_date FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.department_id WHERE hire_date >= '2020-01-01' GROUP BY department_name ORDER BY average_salary DESC; -- ❌ AVOID: Everything on one line SELECT department_name,COUNT(employee_id),AVG(salary),MAX(hire_date) FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.department_id WHERE hire_date >= '2020-01-01' GROUP BY department_name ORDER BY AVG(salary) DESC; Function spacing​ -- ✅ GOOD: Consistent spacing CASE WHEN score >= 90 THEN 'Excellent' WHEN score >= 80 THEN 'Good' WHEN score >= 70 THEN 'Average' ELSE 'Needs Improvement' END AS performance_rating -- ❌ AVOID: Inconsistent spacing CASE WHEN score>=90 THEN'Excellent'WHEN score>=80 THEN 'Good'ELSE'Poor'END

Use appropriate functions​ -- ✅ GOOD: Efficient for large datasets SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) AS order_month, SUM(total_amount) AS monthly_revenue FROM orders GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date); -- ❌ AVOID: Less efficient SELECT SUBSTRING(order_date::text, 1, 7) AS order_month, SUM(total_amount) AS monthly_revenue FROM orders GROUP BY SUBSTRING(order_date::text, 1, 7); Minimize function calls in WHERE clauses​ -- ✅ GOOD: Index-friendly SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date >= '2024-01-01' AND order_date < '2025-01-01'; -- ❌ AVOID: Prevents index usage SELECT * FROM orders WHERE DATE_PART('year', order_date) = 2024;

Always plan for null values​ -- ✅ GOOD: Explicit NULL handling SELECT customer_name, COALESCE(phone_number, 'No phone provided') AS contact_phone, COALESCE(email, 'No email provided') AS contact_email FROM customers; -- ✅ GOOD: Safe division SELECT product_name, CASE WHEN total_orders > 0 THEN ROUND(total_revenue / total_orders, 2) ELSE 0 END AS average_order_value FROM product_summary; COUNT function considerations​ -- ✅ GOOD: Understand the difference SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_rows, -- Counts all rows COUNT(email) AS customers_with_email, -- Counts non-NULL emails COUNT(DISTINCT city) AS unique_cities -- Counts unique non-NULL cities FROM customers;

Consistent data types​ -- ✅ GOOD: Proper type handling SELECT order_id, ROUND(total_amount, 2) AS formatted_total, -- Keep as numeric TO_CHAR(order_date, 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS formatted_date -- Convert to text when needed FROM orders; -- ❌ AVOID: Unnecessary type conversions SELECT order_id::text, -- Unnecessary conversion total_amount::text -- Loses numeric properties FROM orders; Date handling​ -- ✅ GOOD: Timezone aware SELECT order_date, DATE_TRUNC('day', order_date AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS order_day_utc FROM orders; -- ✅ GOOD: Clear date arithmetic SELECT customer_id, registration_date, AGE(CURRENT_DATE, registration_date) AS customer_tenure_days FROM customers;

Clear CASE statements​ -- ✅ GOOD: Comprehensive and readable SELECT employee_id, salary, CASE WHEN salary >= 100000 THEN 'Senior' WHEN salary >= 75000 THEN 'Mid-Level' WHEN salary >= 50000 THEN 'Junior' WHEN salary >= 30000 THEN 'Entry-Level' ELSE 'Intern' END AS salary_band, CASE WHEN department_id IS NULL THEN 'Unassigned' ELSE department_name END AS department_display FROM employees; Nested functions​ -- ✅ GOOD: Logical nesting with comments SELECT customer_id, -- Clean and format customer names INITCAP( TRIM( COALESCE(customer_name, 'Unknown Customer') ) ) AS formatted_customer_name FROM customers;

Meaningful grouping​ -- ✅ GOOD: Clear grouping logic SELECT DATE_TRUNC('quarter', order_date) AS quarter, product_category, COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS unique_customers, COUNT(order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(order_total) AS total_revenue, AVG(order_total) AS average_order_value, STDDEV(order_total) AS revenue_volatility FROM orders o JOIN products p ON o.product_id = p.product_id WHERE order_date >= '2024-01-01' GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('quarter', order_date), product_category HAVING COUNT(order_id) >= 10 -- Only include categories with significant volume ORDER BY quarter DESC, total_revenue DESC;

Self-documenting queries​ -- ✅ GOOD: Clear purpose and logic -- Customer Lifetime Value Analysis -- Calculates CLV for customers active in the last 2 years SELECT c.customer_id, c.customer_name, -- Customer tenure in days AGE(CURRENT_DATE, c.registration_date) AS customer_age_days, -- Purchase behavior metrics COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(o.order_total) AS lifetime_revenue, AVG(o.order_total) AS average_order_value, -- Recency calculation AGE(CURRENT_DATE, MAX(o.order_date)) AS days_since last order, -- Customer lifetime value estimate CASE WHEN COUNT(o.order_id) > 0 THEN ROUND( SUM(o.order_total) / NULLIF(AGE(CURRENT_DATE, c.registration_date), 0) * 365, 2 ) ELSE 0 END AS estimated_annual_value FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.registration_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '2 years' GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_name, c.registration_date HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 0 -- Only customers with purchases ORDER BY estimated_annual_value DESC;

Defensive programming​ -- ✅ GOOD: Prevent division by zero and handle edge cases SELECT product_id, product_name, total_inventory, total_sold, -- Safe percentage calculation CASE WHEN total_inventory > 0 THEN ROUND((total_sold::decimal / total_inventory) * 100, 2) ELSE 0 END AS sell_through_percentage, -- Safe average calculation CASE WHEN order_count > 0 THEN ROUND(total_revenue / order_count, 2) ELSE 0 END AS average order value FROM product_metrics; Input validation​ -- ✅ GOOD: Validate and clean inputs SELECT customer_id, -- Clean phone numbers REGEXP_REPLACE( REGEXP_REPLACE(phone, '[^0-9]', '', 'g'), -- Remove non-digits '^1?(.{10})$', '\1' ) AS cleaned_phone, -- Validate email format CASE WHEN email ~ '^[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}$' THEN LOWER(TRIM(email)) ELSE NULL END AS validated_email FROM customers;

Data quality checks​ -- ✅ GOOD: Include data validation in your queries SELECT 'Customer Data Quality' AS report_type, COUNT(*) AS total_customers, COUNT(CASE WHEN email IS NOT NULL THEN 1 END) AS customers_with_email, COUNT(CASE WHEN phone IS NOT NULL THEN 1 END) AS customers_with_phone, COUNT(CASE WHEN registration_date > CURRENT_DATE THEN 1 END) AS future registration dates, AVG(CASE WHEN customer_name IS NOT NULL THEN LENGTH(customer_name) END) AS avg_name_length FROM customers;

What not to do​ -- ❌ AVOID: Using functions unnecessarily WHERE UPPER(status) = 'ACTIVE' -- Instead create index on status and use = 'ACTIVE' -- ❌ AVOID: Complex nested subqueries when JOINs work better SELECT * FROM customers WHERE customer_id IN ( SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE order_date IN ( SELECT MAX(order_date) FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id ) ); -- ❌ AVOID: Not handling NULLs in aggregations AVG(rating) -- Might not behave as expected with NULLs -- ❌ AVOID: Hardcoded values without context WHERE status_code = 3 -- Use meaningful names: WHERE status = 'ACTIVE'

Before deploying your query, ensure to check the following: Column names are clear and descriptive Functions have meaningful aliases Code is properly formatted and indented NULL values are explicitly handled Data types are appropriate and consistent Performance implications are considered Edge cases (division by zero, empty sets) are handled Comments explain complex logic Query has been tested with sample data Results are validated for accuracy

Review the following before deploying the query: WHERE clauses don't prevent index usage Appropriate functions are used for data types Aggregations are efficient Complex calculations are broken into readable steps Query execution plan has been reviewed

This document provides a comprehensive reference for Apache Spark formulas supported in DataGOL. These formulas enable powerful data processing, analysis, and transformation capabilities directly within your DataGOL workflows.

Data aggregation: Calculate sums, averages, counts, and statistical measures Text processing: Clean, format, and manipulate string data Date/Time operations: Parse, format, and calculate with dates and timestamps Conditional logic: Implement business rules and data validation Data type conversion: Transform data between different formats Array/JSON processing: Handle complex nested data structures Mathematical operations: Perform calculations and statistical analysis

Use appropriate data types - Cast data early in your pipeline. Filter early - Apply WHERE conditions before complex calculations. Avoid nested functions - Break complex formulas into steps. Use COALESCE - Handle nulls explicitly to avoid errors.

Data cleaning: TRIM(UPPER(COALESCE(field, 'DEFAULT'))) Age calculation: DATE_DIFF(CURRENT_DATE(), birth_date) / 365 Categorization: Use CASE WHEN for business logic. Null handling: Always consider null values in calculations.
Use TRY_* functions for safe operations: TRY_DIVIDE, TRY_TO_NUMBER. Test formulas with sample data before production use. Validate data types and ranges.

Category Primary use Key functions Aggregation Summarize data COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX Text Processing Clean/format strings CONCAT, TRIM, UPPER, REPLACE Date/Time Handle temporal data DATE_ADD, DATE_DIFF, EXTRACT Conditional Business logic IF, CASE WHEN, COALESCE Conversion Data type changes CAST, TO_DATE, STRING Mathematical Calculations ROUND, ABS, POWER, MOD Pattern Matching Find/replace patterns LIKE, REGEXP_REPLACE Array/JSON Complex data types SIZE, GET, FLATTEN This reference provides the foundation for powerful data processing in DataGOL using Apache Spark. Start with simple formulas and gradually combine them for more complex data transformations.

Purpose:​ Count rows or non-null values. Usage:​ * COUNT(column_name) * COUNT(*) Example:​ Returns number of customers COUNT(customer_id) Use Case:​ Calculate total records, active users, or non-empty fields.

Purpose:​ Calculate the total of numeric values. Usage:​ SUM(column_name) Example:​ Returns total sales revenue SUM(sales_amount) Use Case:​ Use for financial totals, quantity calculations, or performance metrics.

Purpose:​ Calculate the average value of a set of numbers. Usage:​ * AVG(column_name) * MEAN(column_name) Example:​ Returns average order size AVG(order_value) Use Case:​ Useful for performance benchmarks, trend analysis, and KPI calculations.

Purpose:​ Find the minimum or maximum values within a dataset. Usage:​ * MIN(column_name) * MAX(column_name) Example:​ Returns the latest transaction date MAX(transaction_date) Use Case:​ Apply for data quality checks, range analysis, and finding extremes.

Purpose:​ Find the middle value in sorted data. Usage:​ MEDIAN(column_name) Example:​ Returns the middle salary value MEDIAN(salary) Use Case:​ Good for statistical analysis, outlier detection, and fair comparisons.

Purpose:​ Calculate exact percentile values from a dataset. Usage:​ PERCENTILE(column_name, percentile_value) Example:​ Returns the 95th percentile response time PERCENTILE(response_time, 0.95) Use Case:​ Crucial for performance SLAs, quality metrics, and distribution analysis.

Purpose:​ Join strings together. Usage:​ * CONCAT(str1, str2) * CONCAT_WS(separator, str1, str2) Example:​ Returns "John Smith" CONCAT_WS(' ', first_name, last_name) Use Case:​ Use to create full names, build identifiers, or format display text.

Purpose:​ Change the text case of a string. Usage:​ * UPPER(text) * LOWER(text) Example:​ Returns "USA" UPPER(country_code) Use Case:​ Useful for data standardization and case-insensitive comparisons.

Purpose:​ Remove leading/trailing spaces from a string. Usage:​ TRIM(text) Example:​ Returns clean customer names TRIM(customer_name) Use Case:​ Primarily used for data cleaning and removing extra whitespace.

Purpose:​ Extract part of a string. Usage:​ SUBSTRING(text, start_position, length) Example:​ Returns the area code from a phone number SUBSTRING(phone_number, 1, 3) Use Case:​ Effective for extracting codes, parsing structured text, and data validation.

Purpose:​ Replace specific text patterns within a string. Usage:​ REPLACE(text, old_value, new_value) Example:​ Removes dashes from a phone number REPLACE(phone, '-', '') Use Case:​ Common for data cleaning and format standardization.

Purpose:​ Split a string into an array of substrings. Usage:​ SPLIT(text, delimiter) Example:​ Returns an array of address parts SPLIT(full_address, ',') Use Case:​ Ideal for parsing delimited data and extracting components.

Purpose:​ Check if text contains specific patterns or prefixes. Usage:​ * CONTAINS(text, pattern) * STARTSWITH(text, prefix) Example:​ Returns TRUE/FALSE indicating if an email contains "@gmail.com" CONTAINS(email, '@gmail.com') Use Case:​ Used for data filtering, pattern matching, and validation.

Purpose:​ Get the current date/time. Usage:​ * CURRENT_DATE() * CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() Example:​ Returns the current date, e.g., 2023-01-01 CURRENT_DATE() Use Case:​ Useful to timestamp records, calculate age, or track processing time.

Purpose:​ Add days to a date or calculate the difference between two dates. Usage:​ * DATE_ADD(date, days) * DATE_DIFF(end_date, start_date) Example:​ Returns the number of days since an order DATE_DIFF(order_date, CURRENT_DATE()) Use Case:​ Good for calculating aging, setting due dates, and measuring durations.

Purpose:​ Format dates as strings according to a specified pattern. Usage:​ DATE_FORMAT(date, format) Example:​ Returns "2023-01" DATE_FORMAT(order_date, 'yyyy-MM') Use Case:​ Helpful for display formatting, grouping by period, and reporting.

Purpose:​ Extract specific components (e.g., year, month) from a date. Usage:​ * EXTRACT(part FROM date) * DATE_PART(part, date) Example:​ Returns the year from an order date, e.g., 2023 EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_date) Use Case:​ Essential for time-based analysis and grouping by periods.

Purpose:​ Get the last day of the month for a given date. Usage:​ LAST_DAY(date) Example:​ Returns the last day of the order month LAST_DAY(order_date) Use Case:​ Useful for month-end calculations and defining period boundaries.

Purpose:​ Apply simple conditional logic. Usage:​ IF(condition, true_value, false_value) Example:​ Categorizes based on sales: 'High' if sales > 1000, else 'Low' IF(sales > 1000, 'High', 'Low') Use Case:​ Used for data categorization, flag creation, and implementing business rules.

Purpose:​ Apply multiple condition logic. Usage:​ CASE WHEN condition1 THEN value1 WHEN condition2 THEN value2 ELSE default END Example:​ Assigns a grade based on score: 'A' for >= 90, 'B' for >= 80, else 'C' CASE WHEN score >= 90 THEN 'A' WHEN score >= 80 THEN 'B' ELSE 'C' END Use Case:​ Ideal for complex categorization, multi-tier logic, and scoring systems.

Purpose:​ Return the first non-null value from a list. Usage:​ COALESCE(value1, value2, default) Example:​ Returns the mobile phone, home phone, or 'No Phone' if both are null COALESCE(mobile_phone, home_phone, 'No Phone') Use Case:​ Helps to handle missing data, provide defaults, and ensure data completeness.

Purpose:​ Return null if two values are equal. Usage:​ NULLIF(value1, value2) Example:​ Returns NULL if the discount is 0 NULLIF(discount, 0) Use Case:​ Useful for converting zeros to nulls or creating conditional nulls.

Purpose:​ Convert between different data types. Usage:​ * INT(value) * FLOAT(value) * STRING(value) * BOOLEAN(value) Example:​ Converts sales_amount to an integer INT(sales_amount) Use Case:​ Ensures data type consistency, enables calculations, and aids in data validation.

Purpose:​ Parse strings into date or timestamp values. Usage:​ TO_DATE(date_string, format) Example:​ Converts '2023-01-01' to a date value TO_DATE('2023-01-01', 'yyyy-MM-dd') Use Case:​ Useful for importing data, parsing text dates, and data integration.

Purpose:​ Round numbers in various ways. Usage:​ * ROUND(number, decimals) * CEIL(number) * FLOOR(number) Example:​ Rounds price to 2 decimal places ROUND(price, 2) Use Case:​ Applied in financial calculations, display formatting, and data binning.

Purpose:​ Get the absolute value of a number or its negation. Usage:​ * ABS(number) * NEGATIVE(number) Example:​ Returns an always positive value for profit_loss ABS(profit_loss) Use Case:​ Used for distance calculations and magnitude analysis.

Purpose:​ Calculate the remainder after division. Usage:​ MOD(number, divisor) Example:​ Returns the last digit of an ID MOD(customer_id, 10) Use Case:​ Useful for data sampling, identifying cyclic patterns, and partitioning.

Purpose:​ Calculate the power of a number or its square root. Usage:​ * POWER(base, exponent) * SQRT(number) Example:​ Returns the side length of a square from its area SQRT(area) Use Case:​ Common in scientific calculations and geometric formulas.

Purpose:​ Work with array data. Usage:​ * SIZE(array) * GET(array, index) * CONTAINS(array, value) Example:​ Returns the number of tags in an array SIZE(tags_array) Use Case:​ Used to handle multi-value fields, analyze lists, and perform data validation.

Purpose:​ Convert nested arrays into a single array. Usage:​ FLATTEN(nested_array) Example:​ Converts nested categories into a single list FLATTEN(categories) Use Case:​ Helps to simplify complex data and prepare it for analysis.

Purpose:​ Extract data from JSON objects. Usage:​ * GET_JSON_OBJECT(json, path) * FROM_JSON(json, schema) Example:​ Extracts the email from user data in JSON format GET_JSON_OBJECT(user_data, '$.email') Use Case:​ Crucial for API data processing and semi-structured data analysis.

Purpose:​ Perform pattern matching (case-sensitive or insensitive). Usage:​ * LIKE(text, pattern) * ILIKE(text, pattern) Example:​ Checks if product_name contains "iPhone" LIKE(product_name, '%iPhone%') Use Case:​ Used for text search, data filtering, and pattern detection.

Purpose:​ Perform regular expression matching and manipulation. Usage:​ REGEXP_REPLACE(text, pattern, replacement) Example:​ Removes non-numeric characters from a phone number, leaving only numbers REGEXP_REPLACE(phone, '[^0-9]', '') Use Case:​ Essential for data cleaning, format validation, and complex text processing.

The following new features and enhancements are in this release:

Custom Agent: Date time tool Introducing a Date Time tool for the Custom Agent to interpret and resolve time-based expressions. The following new features and enhancements are in this release:

The following enhancements have been made for Pipelines: Unified pipeline view: The pipeline view has been streamlined by removing the concept of parent/child pipelines. Now, everything (status, error logs, and more) is available directly from a single, unified Pipeline page, making it easier to manage and monitor data streams. Pipeline-level actions: To simplify execution and ensure consistency, the ability to run or cancel individual streams has been removed. Users now manage the entire pipeline as a single unit, which helps prevent fragmented runs and ensures that all active streams are processed together. Last sync column: A new column has been added to the Streams tab to show the last time each stream is completed. This gives a quick and clear overview of the most recent activity for each stream, helping to identify which ones might be out of date. Revamped job table: The Job Table has been redesigned to provide more clarity. Each job can now be expanded to see a comprehensive list of all streams that were included in that run, along with their individual statuses. This gives a complete, at-a-glance overview of the pipeline's activity. "Fix Error" button in the Job table: For custom and deduplication pipeline streams, a new "Fix Error" button is available in the expanded Job Table. This allows users to edit and save queries for failed streams directly from the job view, so issues can be resolved quickly without leaving the page. Retry Last Job button: You can now retry a failed or canceled job with a single click. The new Retry Last Job button will automatically rerun all streams that were active in the last job, helping to get back on track faster.

Unstructured pipeline metadata enhancement for RAG agent: The unstructured pipelines have been enriched with the following new metadata for each chunk: File ID: A unique identifier for the source document, ensuring direct traceability. Document Title: The original title of the source document, providing immediate context. Reference Link: A direct link back to the source document, allowing for easy navigation and verification. This improvement provides a more robust and context-aware retrieval process, enabling better traceability and seamless navigation to the source files.

Enhanced chart classification: The BI Agent’s chart classification logic has been refined to better interpret user queries. This improvement results in charts that are more accurate, relevant, and aligned with both user intent and the available data.

JDBC provider exception shown with user-friendly error messages: Joining multiple data sources is not supported with the JDBC provider. When a user attempts this, an exception is now handled to display a user-friendly error message instead of a technical one. Table response now returns S3 URL: For tables with an associated pipeline, the table response now includes an S3 URL. Improved dynamic workbook joining: Dynamic workbook joining has been improved to better handle changes in parent workbooks. Renaming a column in a parent workbook will no longer break the joined workbook. Additionally, deleting a column that is not used in the final output will not cause the joined workbook to fail. The following are known limitations: Renaming columns that are part of the join condition will still cause the resultant workbook to break. Deleting columns that are part of the join condition or final projection will also break the resultant workbook. The Impact Analysis feature is updated to accurately highlight the changes that will affect the joined workbook before you make them, which helps you manage these limitations.

The following new features and enhancements are in this release:

The new cluster configuration feature provides a multi-level system for managing the compute resources used by data pipelines and other workloads. This allows for precise control over resource allocation to help optimize for both performance and cost. How does it work?​ The system applies a configuration hierarchy to determine the resources for each job. Specific configurations take precedence over more general ones: Pipeline-level override: You can now set specific configurations for individual pipelines, which will override any company-level or default settings. This is ideal for fine-tuning performance on critical jobs. Company-level defaults: A new company-specific configuration can be set to provide a custom default for all pipelines within your organization. This is useful for standardizing resource allocation and ensuring consistency. Parent pipeline inheritance: For orchestrated jobs, child pipelines without a specific configuration will now inherit the settings from their parent pipeline, streamlining complex workflows. Dedicated node groups: For pipelines requiring specific hardware, you can now select dedicated node groups (e.g., 'Medium', 'Large') and define the number of executors for guaranteed resource allocation. Cache handling: The system now intelligently handles configuration updates, ensuring new pipeline runs use the latest settings after a cache refresh. Existing pipelines will continue to use their original snapshot configuration, preventing unexpected changes to in-flight jobs. Job-specific metadata: All configuration details, including overrides, are now stored in the job metadata, providing full transparency and traceability for every run. Specialized workloads: The system now recognizes and applies specific configurations for various workloads, including Playground queries, Workbook/BI queries, and ETL jobs, to ensure each runs with the most suitable resources.

You can now gain granular control over the compute resources allocated to your pipelines. A new UI section is introduced for the pipeline configuration screen that allows you to directly define the cluster size and scaling options for your jobs. This new feature gives you the flexibility to: Select cluster size. You can now choose from predefined cluster types (e.g., small, medium, large) to match your pipeline's specific performance requirements. Set node scaling. You can define the minimum and maximum number of nodes for a job. This allows you to guarantee a baseline of resources for consistent performance while also enabling cost-effective auto-scaling for variable workloads. These configurations are stored at the pipeline level, giving you precise control over each of your jobs.

This version is designed to understand your natural language requests and turn them into validated SQL queries. How does it work? The SQL agent takes your request in plain English and automatically figures out what you're trying to do. It looks at the available data sources, tables, and columns, and then uses that information to create the correct SQL query for you. This means you no longer have to manually look up table and column names or remember complex syntax. The agent uses a sophisticated process to ensure accuracy and efficiency: Intent parsing: It first understands your request and breaks it down into a structured plan. Metadata retrieval: It then pulls information about your data from the system, including descriptions and relationships between tables. Query generation: It uses this information to create a logical plan and write the SQL query for you. Validation: Finally, it validates the generated query to make sure it is correct and ready to use. This new agent simplifies the query writing process, making it faster and more intuitive to get the data you need. It also supports complex instructions, like switching data sources, filtering data, and grouping results. Workbooks​ The new Peek-a-Link feature allows you to view linked rows directly from any column. Previously, you could only see linked data by clicking the link column itself. These updates make it easier to create complex joins and compare data between workbooks.

By separating the Python Agent's execution environment, we ensure that resource-intensive data operations are now handled independently. Benefits Improved scalability and concurrency: Heavy data processing tasks no longer compete for resources with core services, allowing the system to handle a higher volume of parallel operations. Automated cleanup of Iceberg snapshots for full data refresh syncs: Once a full refresh job completes and a new, current snapshot is created, the system will automatically execute a cleanup operation. This guarantees that only the snapshot created by the current, successful FULL_REFRESH job is preserved, effectively mimicking a clean slate while leveraging Iceberg's transactional guarantees. Optimized storage: Automatically reclaims storage space consumed by outdated data files and metadata. Simplified data history: Keeps the table's history clean and focused on relevant, recent snapshots. Reduced manual intervention: Eliminates the need for manual cleanup commands after full refresh operations. Ambiguous date filtering for "Last Week" vs. "Last 7 Days"**​ In the DC Agent, the date filtering logic has been updated to distinguish between calendar periods and rolling windows. Previously, terms like "last week" or "last year" defaulted to a rolling window (e.g., the last 7 or 365 days). Now, the system recognizes "last week" as the specific Monday to Sunday calendar week and "last year" as January 1st to December 31st. Rolling windows are now only triggered when the user explicitly specifies a number of days (e.g., "last 7 days"). For example, a request for "last week" should return data from the most recent completed Monday–Sunday cycle. Instead, if asked on a Wednesday, the system would return data from the previous Wednesday to the current Tuesday. Similarly, a request for "last year" was being treated as "past 365 days" rather than the specific calendar period of January 1st to December 31st of the previous year. This has been corrected to distinguish between Calendar Periods (e.g., "last week" now fetches Monday to Sunday) and Rolling Windows (e.g., "last 7 days" fetches the previous 168 hours). Similarly, "last year" now correctly maps to the previous calendar year rather than a rolling 365-day count. Calendar Periods ("Last Week", "Last Year"): Last Week: Now strictly filters from Monday to Sunday of the previous week. Last Year: Now strictly filters from January 1st to December 31st of the previous year. Rolling Windows ("Last 7 Days", "Last 365 Days"): The system will only use a rolling window from the current timestamp if the user explicitly specifies the number of days (e.g., "last 7 days" or "last 365 days").

Introduced the GRC (Governance, Risk, and Compliance) Agent, a powerful AI collaborator designed to automate and simplify the auditing process. The GRC Agent enables organizations to evaluate their internal policies or third-party vendor documents against established industry standards and regulatory frameworks. GRC use cases​ The following are some use cases of the GRC agent: Access control audits: Verifying if a company follows the "Principle of Least Privilege" or if Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) is strictly enforced. Password policy evaluation: Checking if a company's password requirements (length, complexity, rotation) match the master standard. Vendor risk management: A governing body or large corporation can use the agent to evaluate the security policies of third-party vendors before onboarding them. Internal compliance health checks: Companies can run their own policies against updated international standards to find and fix "gaps" before a formal audit. Key features​ Automated rule extraction: Upload a control file (a list of requirements), and the agent will automatically parse and extract individual compliance rules to be tested. Dual-source comparison: The agent performs a side-by-side analysis between your Standards (the source of truth) and your Target Documents (the policies being audited). AI-generated gap analysis: For every non-compliant or partially compliant rule, the agent provides a detailed description of the gap explaining exactly what is missing or insufficient in the target document. Evidence-based reporting: Every result includes Key Evidences, providing direct references and excerpts from the analyzed documents to support audit findings. Risk scoring dashboard: Get an immediate high-level view of your compliance health with an overall percentage score and a breakdown of Critical, High, and Low-priority risks.

Querying on Salesforce or HubSpot directly results in an error or a failed validation check​ Currently, the SQL Playground allows users to select REST API-based data sources directly. However, because these platforms (Salesforce, HubSpot, etc.) are built on REST APIs rather than standard SQL databases, direct SQL execution is not supported and will result in an error or a failed validation check. Why this happens​ REST connectors act as bridges to pull data; they do not function as queryable database engines. To perform SQL analysis on data from these sources, you must follow the standard ELT (Extract, Load, Transform) workflow: Extract and load: Use an Airbyte sync to pull data from the REST API source. Move to supported destination: Move that data into a supported destination warehouse (such as Parquet or Iceberg). Run query: Navigate to the SQL Playground and run your queries against the Warehouse tables, not the raw Source connectors. Currenlty a validation check is implemented within the Playground to prevent users from attempting direct queries on these sources. This will provide clearer feedback and guide users toward the correct data warehouse tables.

Fixed a critical bug where create_dataframe would fail with a 401 Unauthorized error when executed via a background worker thread (ThreadPoolExecutor). The background worker threads now correctly inherit the necessary Authorization headers, ensuring that internal API calls succeed regardless of which thread executes the task. Addressed a sorting anomaly where tickets marked as Deployed were being incorrectly categorized or omitted from specific status buckets. Fixed an issue where the Jira Agent would occasionally conflate details between different tickets or user sessions. The agent now maintains a clean, accurate memory state.
Date released: March 06, 2026

Refined how workbooks are displayed within the LLM settings to ensure a more intuitive user experience when handling shared resources. Improved workbook display logic Previously, when an agent was shared but the associated workbook was not, the system would display the technical Workbook ID in the LLM settings. This often caused confusion for users who were not familiar with internal ID strings. Enhanced user clarity The interface now provides a clearer state or fallback name, ensuring that users can identify their configuration context without needing to parse raw identification data.
Date released: February 24, 2026

Automated service account integration for public agents: The process for managing agent permissions has been streamlined. When a custom agent is configured for external access, the system now automatically creates the service account and attaches the workspace, eliminating manual configuration. Automatic provisioning: Enabling external access triggers the immediate creation of a dedicated service account. Workspace synchronization: The service account is automatically attached to all workspaces associated with the agent. Dynamic updates: When an agent is updated with new workspaces, the service account permissions are silently refreshed to include the latest workspace list. Clean interface: Service accounts remain hidden from the Team and Workspace views to maintain a decluttered administrative environment. Support for Claude 4.6 Sonnet is now available. This update provides a significant boost in reasoning, coding proficiency, and instruction following while maintaining high execution speeds. Expanded file support for knowledge graph creation: The Knowledge Graph agent is updated to support a wider range of file formats. This expansion allows for more comprehensive data ingestion and more detailed entity relationship mapping. Following are the new supported formats: Structured data: Full support for Excel (.xlsx) and improved parsing for large JSON and CSV datasets. Document types: Added support for Rich Text (.rtf) and OpenDocument (.odt) files. Concurrent public link support: Enhanced session management now enables the opening of multiple public links within the same browser. This update introduces multi-session support for public links, allowing multiple agent or application instances to run simultaneously in the same browser without session conflicts.

Fixed an issue where selecting a specific model within a Custom Agent configuration would fail to propagate to the chat interface. Chats will now correctly honor the model parameters defined at the agent level rather than defaulting to the system standard. Fixed Broken Agent Share Links: Resolved a critical issue where public thread links generated for Custom Agents were resulting in a 404 "We could not find a match" error.
Date released: March 10, 2026
Pipeline Job Metrics: Pipeline jobs now display bytes emitted, giving better visibility into data processing and performance.
Improved Athena Workbook Stability Restored smooth "Auto" option selection on Single Select columns in Athena Workbook, while fully retaining the latest Athena performance enhancements.

New User Welcome Email New users now receive an automated welcome email upon account creation, providing a direct link to access their DataGOL account. The email introduces role-based guidance — helping both business users and stakeholders get started with DataGOL's AI agents to self-serve insights independently.

Fixed an issue where nested formulas failed to execute after a recent update that changed column quoting behavior to wrap all column names in double quotes unconditionally. The new quoting logic generated invalid SQL when a formula referenced another formula column, causing the backend to throw an exception. Column quoting has been corrected to ensure valid SQL is produced for both base and nested formula references.
Date released: March 11, 2026

Revamped Explore Page The Explore page has been redesigned to improve agent discoverability and help users find the right agent faster. Key improvements include: Category Filters — Browse agents by capability using quick filter buttons (e.g., Advanced Reasoning, Intelligence & Search, Analytics & Insight, Integration & Action, Custom). Search Support — Find agents instantly using the new search input. About this Agent Modal — Click to open a detailed description of each agent's capabilities and recommended use cases, keeping the card UI clean and uncluttered. Improved Agent Card Layout — Refreshed presentation for a cleaner, more scannable experience. Simplified Custom Agent Interface - Workbook, Data Source, and Workspace dropdowns have been removed to reduce clutter. Users can now add context or resources using the universal “+” button, creating a cleaner and more intuitive workflow across all agents.

Guided Onboarding Tour A step-by-step product tour now automatically launches for first-time users upon entering the platform, helping them quickly understand core features and get to their first interaction faster. Key improvements include: Guided UI Walkthrough — The tour highlights key areas of the interface, including Workspaces and Documents, to help new users orient themselves quickly. Agent Introduction — Agents are introduced as a primary interaction point, with contextual guidance on where and how to use them. First Question Prompt — The final step of the tour encourages users to ask their first question, enabling them to immediately experience the core value of the platform. Ask from Home Page — Users can now ask questions directly from the home page without navigating to another section. Skippable Tour — Users can exit or skip the tour at any point if they prefer to explore independently.
Date released: March 13, 2026

Improved Query Execution for DAVE and DCA agent Queries run through DAVE and DCA now use the Playground endpoint, removing workbook-specific restrictions and allowing queries to be copied directly into the Playground without modification. Improved GTM Agent Column Output The GTM Agent's column output configuration now dynamically structures the response to match the target workbook, ensuring results are consistently formatted and ready for use without manual adjustment. AI Connectors Manual Re-indexing Users can now manually trigger re-indexing directly within AI Connectors. Flexible Agent Configuration Featured Agents can now be configured to match your team's specific needs — with settings that adapt based on the agent type and are saved per company. This makes it easier to customize how agents behave, what tools they use, and how they deliver results, all from a single dedicated settings page.
Fixed Query Publishing to Workspace Resolved an issue where publishing a query to a workspace failed due to queryEditorId being passed as null.
Date released: March 18, 2026

Atlassian Agent (Jira + Confluence Unified): Introduced a new unified Atlassian Agent that combines Jira and Confluence capabilities into a single conversational interface. You can now ask questions about Jira issues, sprint progress, and Confluence pages all in one place, with no need to switch between separate agents. Improved performance by addressing response slowness, resulting in faster query turnaround when working with Jira and Confluence data.

Domain-based signup restrictions: Admins can now restrict who can sign up by configuring an allowed list of email domains. Only users with approved domains can register via self-signup or Google sign-in, while invite-based signups are always permitted regardless of domain. Google sign-in error handling has also been improved for a more consistent experience.
Updated NetSuite JDBC connector to use NetSuite2.com as the ServerDataSource, replacing the deprecated NetSuite.com endpoint.

Resolved multiple stability and response quality issues in the newly launched Atlassian Agent. Fixed several issues in the GTM Agent affecting query execution and output formatting. Eliminated a duplicate entry issue in the Conversation List where the same conversation could appear more than once after certain interactions. Fixed a bug where the connector was not auto-selected after successful OAuth authorization. Resolved an issue causing the Jira Agent to respond slowly. Queries and data retrieval are now significantly faster.
Date released: March 20, 2026

Company-wide thread sharing: Threads can now be shared at the company level. Once enabled, threads automatically appear in the thread section for all users within the same company domain — no manual sharing required. GRC Agent — Source chunk visibility for non-compliant controls: The GRC Agent now surfaces the exact source and target document chunks behind every non-compliant or partially-compliant control finding. Results are stored directly in your output workbook, making it easier to: Trace evidence back to the original source Annotate and review findings in context Share audit-ready documentation with stakeholders RAG Agent: Faster, More Accurate Responses: Removed the planning phase from the RAG Agent pipeline. This phase was introducing unnecessary latency and occasionally degrading response accuracy. RAG queries are now faster and more direct. Custom Agent — Public document download control: Added a new "Allow Public Document Downloads" toggle in the Custom Agent settings. When enabled, external users accessing a public agent can download associated documents; when disabled, download options are hidden for public users. Internal and explicitly shared users are unaffected and always retain download access.

Agents now accessible to all users: Fixed an issue where users without certain permissions were being redirected back to the Home page after submitting a question, causing their message to be lost. Agents are now accessible to all users with no interruptions or redirect loops.
Date released: March 23, 2026

Python Agent - Auto Approve Mode: Added an Auto Approve toggle to the Python Agent. When enabled, the agent skips all confirmation prompts, including plan/code review and mid-query clarification requests, and executes end-to-end automatically. When disabled, the existing interactive feedback workflow remains unchanged. This is ideal for trusted, repeatable queries where speed matters more than step-by-step review.

Workbook timestamps now show seconds and milliseconds: Timestamp columns in the Workbook now display full precision (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.SSS), making it easier to distinguish between rapid back-to-back events and true duplicates. Workbook knowledge graph — entity names now shown upfront: Node labels in the knowledge graph now display the actual entity name (e.g., "John Doe") instead of the generic type (e.g., "Person"), making relationships between entities immediately clear without needing to click for details.
Date released: March 24, 2026

Slack integration now retrieves all channel types: After connecting your Slack account, DataGOL now retrieves public channels, private channels, and external Slack Connect channels. Fellow connector — Super Admin mode: Added a Super Admin toggle when setting up the Fellow connector. When enabled, DataGOL retrieves meeting and transcripts data on behalf of all users in the workspace, giving admins a complete view across the entire organization.

Workbook — Convert linked columns to manual relations: Linked columns can now be converted to manual relations, with all existing matched record pairs automatically carried over. Supports one-to-one, one-to-many, and many-to-many relation types with no data loss during conversion. Workbook — Improved lookup column interactions: Lookup columns now behave consistently with link columns. A + button appears on hover, allowing users to create and attach new links directly from the lookup cell without navigating away from the current view.
Date released: March 26, 2026

Removed Basic Authentication for Atlassian Connector: Basic Authentication (username/password) has been removed as a login option for the Atlassian connector. OAuth 2.0 is now the sole supported authentication method, ensuring a more secure setup process. Document Indexing Status Filter – Workspace: Added a new filter to the Documents tab that lets you quickly identify documents that haven't been indexed yet. You can now see exactly what's still being processed and what's AI ready — giving you full visibility into your document indexing status at a glance.

Faster, Simpler Onboarding with OTP Verification: The account creation flow has been redesigned to reduce friction and get users to value faster. The previous multi-field form and email hash link verification have been replaced with a streamlined OTP-based signup — just enter your email and password, verify with a one-time code, and you're in. A short optional profile step lets you personalize your experience without blocking access.

Fixed an issue where citation links in Custom and RAG agent responses failed to open the referenced workspace document. Users can now click any citation to navigate directly to the source, making it easier to verify information and build confidence in agent responses.
Date released: March 31, 2026

Charts and Dashboards Now Available in Custom Agent: The Frontend Design Skill has been integrated into the Custom Agent, allowing users to generate charts and dashboards directly from their queries for instant visual data insights. Stop a Running Agent Mid-Execution: Users can now cancel an active agent mid-processing, which immediately halts execution and readies the agent to accept a new question. Improved Responsiveness of Frontend Skills in Custom Agent: Performance and layout improvements now make frontend skills render faster and more reliably in the Custom Agent, with added support for more customized skills to boost agent intelligence and flexibility. More Precise Confluence Permissions for the Atlassian Agent: The Atlassian Agent now uses fine-grained Confluence permission scopes, ensuring it only requests the specific access it needs — improving security and reducing unnecessary permissions. See Non-Compliant Details Directly in the Workbook: The GRC Agent now displays non-compliant content chunk details directly in the workbook during compliance checks, giving users clear visibility into exactly what failed and why. New AI Model Available: OpenAI GPT-5.4: OpenAI's latest model, GPT-5.4, is now available on the platform and can be selected when configuring agents or queries.

See linked records across all lookup columns in one unified view Link two workbooks across different workspaces seamlessly Experience consistent search behavior in expanded popups, just like in workbooks Copy, paste, and bulk add options for single select and multi-select fields Add AI-generated logic directly to static columns Prevent duplicate selections by disabling already-added fields when creating new lookup columns

Index Settings Crash on Unconfigured WorkbookResolved an issue where opening Index Settings on an unconfigured workbook caused the system to error out — the settings page now loads correctly in all states.
Date released: April 1, 2026
Users can now connect Supabase as a data source. Simply provide your connection details including host, port, credentials, and schema to get started.

File URL Redirect in Extraction Tracker: Workspace ID is now visible in the extraction tracker for better traceability. Clicking the File URL now redirects users directly to the corresponding context document.

Sign In with Microsoft: Users can now sign in using their Microsoft account, similar to the existing Google sign-in option. New users are automatically onboarded with an account, while existing users are redirected straight to the home page upon login.

Stop or Cancel a Question Being Processed by the AI Agent Users can now interrupt and cancel a question that the AI Agent is actively working on, without needing to wait for it to finish or refresh the page.

Fixed an issue where the Select All and Deselect All buttons were not functioning on the Atlassian Agent's MCP tool configuration page. Users can now properly select or clear all tools at once when configuring the Atlassian Agent.
Date released: April 03, 2026

Claude Sonnet 4.6 Now Available in Python Agent: Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 4.6 model has been added to the Python Agent's LLM configuration options. Users can now select Claude Sonnet 4.6 when setting up or configuring their Python-based agents.
Security Patch A set of security alerts identified on April 2, 2026 have been reviewed and resolved in this release.

DataGOL columns are now automatically included when copying data into the warehouse. Users can expect consistent column naming aligned with DataGOL conventions across all copied datasets. Automatic Backend Retry for REST Pipelines: The backend now automatically initiates a single retry when a REST pipeline run fails, reducing manual intervention for common failure scenarios. Each failed run gets exactly one backend-created retry, with safeguards to prevent duplicate retries if a user has already triggered one. In orchestrated pipelines, downstream jobs are triggered only after the retried run completes successfully.
Date released: April 06, 2026
New HubSpot Agent: Launched HubSpot Agent in Alpha, providing early access to HubSpot-native AI automation capabilities within the platform.

PDF Template Generation for Attachment Columns: Added support for PDF generation using attachment column templates. Users can now upload document templates, configure dynamic output file naming, and generate PDFs for single or bulk records through dedicated APIs. Bulk PDF generation supports asynchronous processing with request status tracking for improved scalability and monitoring.

Centralized Help Center: Added a new in-platform Help Center with unified access to documentation, walkthroughs, webinars, and support resources. Enhanced search capabilities and categorized learning sections enable users to find relevant guidance and product information faster. Global Announcement Banner: Added a platform-wide announcement banner for time-sensitive updates like webinars and product news, with optional links, dismiss persistence, and automatic expiry support.

Fixed a slowness issue in the HubSpot Agent, resulting in faster execution and improved responsiveness for HubSpot workflows. Resolved a CSS leakage issue in Custom Agent HTML responses that was impacting surrounding page styles. Fixed Mongo ingestion issues in multicatalog where NULL values inside nested structures caused void type resolution failures. Added recursive traversal support for complex structs, arrays, and deeply nested fields.
Date released: April 02, 2026

New Charts​ Radial Chart: Compare multiple categories on a circular axis for quick visual ranking and proportional insights. Radar Chart: Plot multi-dimensional metrics across time periods (such as months) or categories using an intuitive spider-web layout. Sunburst Chart: Explore hierarchical data with interactive drill-down navigation, from region to category to subcategory. Cohort Analysis: Build retention heatmaps to track how user groups behave and engage over time. Top N / Bottom N on Grouped Charts: Instantly filter grouped charts to surface only the highest or lowest performing segments. New Feature​ LOD (Level of Detail) lets you compute a metric at a different grouping level than your chart — without changing the chart's existing grouping or layout. For example, you can show total sales by category while simultaneously calculating each category's share of the grand total, a value computed across all data. This makes it possible to blend chart-level and dataset-level calculations in a single visualization.
Date released: April 07, 2026

Workflow Automation Infrastructure: Introduced backend infrastructure to automate end-to-end workflow execution, including data source setup, warehouse and pipeline creation, workspace publishing, and BI page/widget configuration.
Date released: April 08, 2026
Agent & Thread Sharing: Delivered major enhancements to agent and thread sharing, improving reliability, consistency, and overall cross-user collaboration experience.
Date released: April 09, 2026

Custom Agent – Skills: Introduced Skills support for Custom Agents, enabling reusable instruction sets that can be created in the UI or uploaded as Markdown files and shared across the organization for use by multiple agents. Custom Agent - Model Selection: Enhanced Custom Agents to allow different LLM models per subagent, providing finer-grained control beyond the previous agent-level model selection. Custom Agent - Image Responses: Added a configuration toggle in Custom Agents to enable or disable image inclusion in responses, allowing users to switch between image-supported and text-only outputs with saved preferences.

Custom Agent: Fixed an issue where MCP tools configured at the main agent level were not being picked up during execution, ensuring proper tool usage. Atlassian Agent: Resolved multiple issues in the Atlassian Agent, improving overall stability and reliability of Atlassian-related workflows.
Date released: April 17, 2026

Data Science Agent - Multi-Dataset Analysis: Enabled support for multiple datasets in a single chat, allowing users to load and analyze additional workbooks alongside the main dataset for cross-table analysis and comparisons. ds_multi_wb.png Custom Agent – Unsaved Changes Protection: Added a guard to prevent users from leaving pages with unsaved changes in Custom Agent forms, helping avoid accidental data loss.
Allow clearing a date cell in workbooks: Enable users to clear an already-set date value in the grid date editor, by setting the underlying cell value to null.
Date released: April 15, 2026

Python Agent - Groq Model & Analysis Levels: Added Groq model support with configurable analysis levels (Fast, Moderate, Deep) and company-level API key management for flexible performance and integration control.

Workspace Level MCP Support: Extended MCP support from workbook to workspace level, allowing centralized setup and easier integration of workspace MCPs with Custom Agents. Workbook Duplication Enhancements: Enabled workbook duplication with or without data copy, ensuring tables, columns, folders, and views are correctly replicated. All workbook types (dynamic, static, hybrid) are treated as dynamic after duplication for consistency.
Google Spaces Connector: Enabled seamless setup for Google Spaces integration, allowing users to connect their account and automatically ingest messages, spaces, members, and reactions.

Agent Skill Unique Name Validation: Fix Resolved a bug where the uniqueness constraint on Agent Skill names was not being correctly enforced. Skills now correctly prevent duplicate names within the same company scope.
Date released: April 21, 2026

File Preview API for Agent File Attachments: A dedicated file preview API has been introduced for the Agent File Attachment feature. This isolates the downloadable instance of an attached file, improving how attached files are accessed and previewed within the agent chat context. Retry Middleware for Provider Exceptions and Rate Limiting: A new retry middleware layer has been added to the Custom Agent to automatically handle provider-level exceptions and rate limiting. This provides a more robust, infrastructure-level safety net that intercepts and retries failed LLM calls transparently, improving overall agent stability and reliability under load. Duplicate Primary Dataframe Loading at Session Startup: Fixed a bug where the primary workbook's dataframe was being loaded twice during Python Agent session initialization. The duplicate fetch caused unnecessary data retrieval operations, increased startup latency, and redundant resource usage. The session now correctly loads the primary dataset once, while auxiliary workbook loading continues to run in parallel as expected.
Date released: April 20, 2026

Custom Agent - File Attachments: Attach Files to Chat and Ask Questions About Them Users can now attach files directly to a Custom Agent chat session and ask questions about the file's contents. This enables document-driven conversations without requiring the file to be pre-loaded into a workbook or data source. Custom Agent - Automated File Parsing: The Read Complete File tool now includes an automated parser that activates when needed. Previously, file content handling required manual configuration; the agent can now automatically determine the appropriate parsing approach based on the file type, improving reliability when working with file-based data. Custom Agent - Automatic Retry on Rate Limiting and Interruptions: The Custom Agent now automatically retries when it encounters rate limiting or other transient interruptions from the underlying LLM provider. This improves agent reliability during high-load periods and reduces the need for users to manually re-run queries that were interrupted.

Agent No Longer Stops Mid-Response Fixed an issue where the Custom Agent would intermittently stop generating a response partway through, leaving incomplete outputs. Responses are now delivered in full consistently. Skills Not Being Read by LocalShellBackend Resolved a bug where Agent Skills were not being picked up when the Custom Agent ran against the LocalShellBackend. Skills are now correctly loaded and applied in all execution environments.
Date released: April 22, 2026

Custom Agent – Conversation Grouping: Improved the Agents side panel by grouping conversations into collapsible time-based sections and also by agent type, making it easier to navigate and manage chat history.

Workbook/Workspace Delete UX: Now we have delete protection enabled for workbook and workspace deletion to avoid accidental deletions. Workbook Append/Import UX: When a user removes a new/unmapped field, they have a clear option to undo the action.
Date released: April 23, 2026

Page-Level Filter: Exclude Weekends A new toggle in the date picker lets you exclude Saturday and Sunday from all dashboard visualizations in one click. Perfect for business metrics where weekend data creates noise in otherwise weekday-driven trends. Embedded Dashboards: DataGOL dashboards can now be embedded into external apps and websites via IFrame, JavaScript Widget, Data Attributes, or React component. Users can interact with analytics directly inside your product without ever logging into DataGOL. Theming for Embedded Dashboards: A new Theme Editor lets you customize tile titles, header backgrounds, font sizes, and colors on embedded dashboards. Match your product's branding seamlessly — accessible from dashboard settings under Theme Editor. Dynamic Parameters (SQL-Driven Dropdowns): Parameter dropdowns can now be auto-populated from a SQL query, keeping filter options always in sync with your data. Users get live-updating dropdowns on dashboards, and values can be referenced in formula columns using {{param}} syntax. Reordering Parameters on Dashboards: Parameters can now be drag-and-drop reordered and toggled visible/hidden directly from Dashboard Page Settings. Gives teams full control over the filter experience presented to end users. Collapse All on Pivot Table Rows: Pivot Tables now include a Collapse All button that folds every row group to the top level instantly. Ideal for high-level summaries — individual groups can still be expanded with the + icon.

Pivot Table Percentage Values Follow Column Reordering: Percentage values in Pivot Tables previously stayed in their original position when columns were reordered. This is now fixed — percentage values correctly follow their associated columns on reorder.
Date released: April 27, 2026

Smarter Conversation Navigation in the Agent Side Panel: Agent conversations are now grouped by time — Today, Yesterday, Last 7 Days, and Older — replacing the previous flat list. This makes it much easier to find and return to past conversations, especially as your history grows. Delete Confirmation Now Requires Name Entry: Deleting a workspace or workbook now requires you to type the item name before the action is enabled, with a clear warning about permanent deletion. This extra step prevents accidental data loss and gives you a moment to confirm you're deleting the right thing.

Each user can now configure their own GTM agent prompt, output settings, and instruction rules independently. This means your GTM agent setup no longer affects or gets overwritten by teammates' configurations.
documents.s: GTM Agent Is Now Personalized Per User

documents.t: You can now stop a running Python (Data Science) agent execution at any time using the new stop control. This gives you more control when a query is taking too long or you need to adjust your approach.

Role-Based Access for External Dashboard Sharing: You can now assign Viewer or Editor permissions when sharing dashboards externally, giving editors the ability to pin and unpin pages collaboratively. This reduces dependency on the original dashboard owner and enables faster, team-driven dashboard maintenance.

Guided Setup Templates for HubSpot, Google Calendar, and Gmail: When you connect HubSpot, Google Calendar, or Gmail, you can now choose a pre-built template to automatically set up your analytics — pipelines, workbook, and dashboard — in one guided flow. A live progress tracker keeps you informed at every step, so you go from connected to insights without any manual configuration. HubSpot Now Generally Available: The HubSpot connector has officially graduated from Alpha and is now fully available on the platform. You can connect HubSpot with confidence knowing it's a stable, supported integration ready for everyday use. Seamless Connector Reconnection When Access Expires: If a connected data source needs to be re-authorized, DataGOL now detects this automatically and prompts you to reconnect — right where you're working. Your existing connector and its settings are preserved throughout the process, so nothing needs to be reconfigured after reconnecting.

Fixed an issue where the selected data source wasn't shown on HubSpot agent threads, leaving it unclear which connector was active. The connector indicator now appears correctly so you always know what's powering your agent.
documents.s: Active Connector Now Visible on HubSpot Agent Threads

documents.t: Agents were appearing in a different order on the Explore page versus the side navigation — this is now fixed. Both views reflect the same ordering, so navigating between them is no longer disorienting.
documents.s: Consistent Agent Ordering Across Explore and Side Nav

documents.t: Date released: April 29, 2026

Agent File Attachments: File Preview API for Agent File Attachments A dedicated file preview API has been introduced for the Agent File Attachment feature. This isolates the downloadable instance of an attached file, improving how attached files are accessed and previewed within the agent chat context. Custom Agent - Google Drive Connector: Custom Agent with Google Drive Connector Custom Agents can now be connected to Google Drive as a data source. This allows agents to access and query content stored in Google Drive directly, enabling knowledge retrieval workflows that leverage existing Drive documents without requiring manual imports or re-uploads. RAG V2 API Integration for Google Drive Connector Indexing: The in-house RAG V2 pipeline has been integrated to handle indexing of content sourced through the Google Drive Connector. This ensures that Google Drive-connected documents are indexed and retrievable through the same performant, in-house retrieval infrastructure introduced for other connector types, replacing any dependency on legacy indexing paths for Drive content.
Date released: May 5, 2026

Custom Agent - Google Cloud Integration: Google Cloud Company Keys Support has been added for Google Cloud company-level keys, enabling organizations to configure and manage their own Google Cloud credentials at the company level. This allows Custom Agents and platform integrations that rely on Google Cloud services to authenticate using company-owned keys rather than shared or default credentials, improving security, accountability, and isolation across tenants. MongoDB Queries Now Run via Spark in Playground: When running queries in the Playground, MongoDB connections are now routed through Spark instead of JDBC. This ensures reliable query execution for MongoDB data sources.
Date released: April 30, 2026

GTM Agent ICP to Company List and People List Flow: The GTM Agent backend has been extended to support an ICP (Ideal Customer Profile) driven research flow. When a user executes ICP research from the Chrome Extension, the agent now processes and routes the output into structured Company List and People List workbooks, enabling downstream usage for targeting, indexing, and further agent-based analysis. GTM ICP Research UI: The GTM Agent Chrome Extension and settings page have been enhanced to support ICP-driven research. Users can now define and save an ICP prompt under the GTM Agent settings, then select ICP as a research type directly from the extension. When selected, the extension automatically fetches the saved ICP prompt and executes the research without requiring manual input, with results written to a structured workbook for further use. PDF Download Button Discoverability in Agent Chat: The PDF download experience within the agent chat interface has been improved. Previously, the download action was represented by a minimal icon-only button inside the right-hand PDF viewer panel, making it difficult to discover. The button has been given a clearer label and improved visual prominence so users can easily identify and access the download action without relying on icon interpretation.
Date released: May 7, 2026
DCA V2: Launched the next version of DCA with enhanced capabilities and performance improvements.
Date released: May 6, 2026

Custom Agent - Security: Shell Command Security for Custom Agents Security hardening has been applied to shell command execution within Custom Agents. Potentially harmful operations have been restricted, including commands related to user addition, unauthorized file reads, and other dangerous system-level instructions. Custom Agents executing shell tools will now block or sanitize these categories of commands, reducing the risk of unintended system access or data exposure during agent execution. Custom Agent - Reliability: Model Retry Middleware for Custom Agents A retry middleware layer has been introduced for model calls within Custom Agents. When a model call fails due to transient errors, the middleware automatically retries the request, improving the overall reliability and resilience of Custom Agent execution without requiring any changes from the user or agent configuration.
Date released: May 7, 2026

Workbook RAG: The workbook knowledge base indexing pipeline has been fully migrated from the external Onyx API to a new in-house RAG pipeline, with the legacy Onyx dependency fully removed. The UI now detects existing connectors and surfaces the right CTA — "Start Indexing" or "Reindex Workbook" — along with live indexing progress, run status, errors, and retry states. Once indexed, workbooks can be attached as a knowledge source to an agent, and reindexing after changes updates the knowledge base content immediately. Toggle to Show/Hide Execution Data in Agent Chat Responses (Custom Agents Only): A configurable toggle has been added to Custom Agent settings to control whether execution data is rendered inline in chat responses, addressing user confusion where execution data was misinterpreted as errors or broken behavior. Located under Custom Agent > Advanced Tab > Chat Interface, the toggle defaults to ON (preserving existing behavior) and when turned OFF, hides execution data from the chat UI while keeping it accessible internally for debugging. Applies only to Custom Agents — Featured Agents always show execution data — and the setting persists per agent with full backward compatibility for existing agents. Streaming Continue Option When Connection Interrupte: A continue option has been introduced for AI streaming responses when a connection is interrupted mid-stream. Users can now resume a response without restarting the entire interaction, improving reliability and experience during unstable network conditions.
Date released: May 7, 2026

Support for AWS Bedrock Models: The Custom Agent now supports AWS Bedrock as a model provider. Users can configure and run agents using Bedrock-hosted models, expanding the available model selection beyond existing providers and enabling teams already invested in the AWS ecosystem to leverage their Bedrock setup directly within the agent platform. Support for Vertex AI Models: Vertex AI models are now supported as a model provider option within the Custom Agent. This allows agents to be configured to use Google Cloud-hosted models via Vertex AI, broadening the provider landscape and giving teams additional flexibility in model selection based on their infrastructure and preference.
Date released: May 11, 2026

Agent UX - Updated Landing Page Design: The AI Space landing page has been refreshed with an updated visual design, improving the overall presentation and first-impression experience when users enter the AI Space. Codex Agent: Prior Thread Data Shown in UI The Codex agent UI now surfaces prior thread data, allowing users to view historical conversation context directly within the interface. This improves continuity across sessions and reduces the need to re-establish context when returning to an ongoing Codex workflow.
Date released: May 14, 2026

Custom Agent - Google Spaces Connector: A new Google Spaces Connector enables Custom Agents to connect to and query Google Spaces conversations via OAuth, syncing messages, thread replies, and full conversation history with both historical and incremental sync support. Individual messages and full thread conversations are treated as distinct retrieval chunks, agent responses include citation links back to the source message or conversation, and date-based filtering is available for synced content.
