Sync history is tracked with cancellation support, thread-level operations (rename, share, open in new tab, delete) are available, and the connector handles large messages and lengthy thread conversations. Metadata Filters for Google Drive Connector: Search precision within the Google Drive Connector has been improved through the addition of metadata filtering. Previously, searches relied solely on the user's query text. Now, searches also incorporate file name, record ID, last updated date, and source URL as metadata. For follow-up questions within a conversation, results are automatically narrowed to the same source document via record ID filtering, ensuring contextual continuity across multi-turn queries.
Date released: May 19, 2026

Tenant Workbook support: Introduced Tenant Workbook support for secure multi-tenant data sharing, enabling DYNAMIC master workbooks to be published into other workspaces with shared physical storage, automatic tenant-based row filtering and write enforcement, live schema inheritance from the master workbook, async cache synchronization, and restricted schema modification on tenant workbooks.
Date released: May 20, 2026

Cloud Storage Agnostic Support for Custom Agent Skills: Custom Agent skills have been updated to support multiple cloud storage providers. Previously, agent skills were exclusively stored in AWS S3. Following the GCP migration, the storage layer has been refactored to be fully storage-agnostic, now supporting: Google Cloud Storage (GCS), Microsoft Azure Blob Storage and Amazon S3
Date released: May 21, 2026

Custom Agent Sharing - Service Account Support: Custom agents can now be shared with Service Accounts. Previously, agent sharing was limited to individual user accounts. This enhancement allows platform and integration teams to assign custom agents to service accounts, enabling automated workflows, system-to-system integrations, and programmatic agent access without relying on individual user credentials.
Added support for Column Filter and Sort support for Lookup Columns
Date released: May 27, 2026

Google Drive Connector - Metadata Support: The Google Drive Connector now includes a dedicated metadata tool that lets the AI answer questions directly about your Drive files — such as how many files exist, who created a specific document, or when a file was last updated. Previously limited to content-based search, the connector can now respond to structural and ownership queries using file metadata including File Name, Record ID, Last Updated Date, and Source URL.

BI Dashboard Admin: A new BI Admin role gives designated users company-wide visibility and control over all External Dashboards — including the ability to view, manage access, and remove pages — without requiring explicit sharing.
Date released: May 28, 2026

Formula Computation On the fly: All formula columns are now computed in real time via CTE at query time, replacing the previous UPDATE-based evaluation that triggered on every row change. This eliminates stale formula values, removes the overhead of physical column writes on each update, and ensures formula results are always accurate and up to date. Backend Performance Improvements: Optimized data loading for tables with relationships to eliminate unnecessary processing, delivering faster response times and improved stability for large datasets.
Date released: May 28, 2026

###AI Enhanced Skill Management: AI services can now seamlessly upload and update skills, making skill management more efficient and automated. This enhancement provides a consistent and streamlined experience for maintaining skills across the platform.

Configurable Web Search Providers for AI Generate: Users can now select their preferred web search provider (Perplexity, Tavily, or Parallel Web Systems) when using AI Generate with web access enabled. The platform securely sends only the selected provider's API key to the AI service and adds support for configuring Parallel Web Systems credentials. AI Generate - Image URL Support: Deployed AI Generate columns can now interpret and analyze images referenced by URL. Users can include URLs that point directly to image files within their AI prompts, and the AI engine will fetch and read the image content as part of the generation process. This enables richer, visually-aware AI responses — for example, extracting data from product images, reading charts or diagrams, or describing visual content — all without needing to upload the image separately.

Resolved a configuration issue that caused not all AI models to be visible in AI Generate settings. The models are now correctly exposed and selectable across environments following a configuration update.
Date released: June 2, 2026

Custom Agents - Conversational Skill Updates: Users can now instruct a Custom Agent to revise and update any of its attached skills directly within the conversation — without leaving the agent thread. If a user invokes a skill and is unsatisfied with its behavior or output, they can describe their expectations in natural language within the same thread or a new one. The agent will autonomously rewrite the skill and apply the update accordingly. This closes the loop between skill usage and skill improvement, enabling a self-refining agent experience.

Resolved an issue where Custom Agents were incorrectly refusing to generate downloadable files (PDF, CSV, XLSX, HTML reports) even when file generation was the expected behavior. Previously, users had to explicitly override the agent's refusal to get it to produce the file. The agent now generates requested files without requiring user intervention. Fixed a connector status issue introduced during the GCS-to-S3 migration. When both GCS and S3 connectors coexisted during the transition, the workspace file status was incorrectly being sourced from S3 instead of GCS. The fix establishes GCS as the preferred connector in such cases, ensuring accurate status reporting. Resolved an authentication bug affecting Anthropic models used within AI Generate columns. The fix ensures proper credential handling so that Anthropic models authenticate correctly during AI Generate execution.
Date released: June 4, 2026

Motion MCP Connector Integration for Custom Agents: Custom Agents now support the Motion MCP connector. Users can create a Motion MCP connector and attach it directly to a Custom Agent during agent creation or configuration. Once connected, the agent answers questions about the user's Motion workspace by making MCP tool calls and generating responses from the returned data. Motion MCP tools are fully available to the agent, and tool call errors are handled gracefully.

Fixed an issue where the Hubspot agent would repeat tool calls multiple times and intermittently return "An error occurred while processing the request" when a thread was shared at the company level or internally shared with editor role access. The agent now responds correctly and efficiently on shared threads. Fixed a performance issue where the Python Agent experienced very long response delays when a thread was shared at the company level or internally with editor role, and the auto-suggestion toggle was disabled. After asking a question and providing feedback on the shared thread, the agent now responds in a timely manner. Fixed a bug where Custom Agents using the Motion MCP Connector were returning results in an error format for certain sets of questions. The agent now processes Motion MCP tool calls correctly and returns proper responses.
Date released: June 5, 2026

Dave Agent — Enhanced Analysis & Visualizations DAVE Fixes: The Dave agent now delivers smarter insights with improved charting, better support for multiple data sources, and new cohort analysis capabilities. These enhancements provide more accurate visualizations and a richer analytics experience. Agent Streaming — Automatic Session Recovery: AI conversations now continue seamlessly even if you refresh the page or switch tabs. Ongoing responses automatically reconnect, ensuring you never lose progress while an agent is working. SQL Agent — Improved Multi-Data Source Support: The SQL Agent now works more effectively across multiple connected data sources, automatically selecting the appropriate configuration for your queries. This improves reliability and provides a smoother experience when working with complex workspaces.

The SQL Playground now supports no-copy workbook references in queries without requiring users to manually inline their SQL definitions. Previously, workbooks without a physical table (no-copy workbooks) could not be referenced directly in a playground query, forcing users to copy-paste the underlying SQL definition as a CTE manually. The backend now automatically detects no-copy workbook references, recursively expands them into CTEs in dependency order, and prepends the WITH block to the query before execution.
Date released: June 5, 2026

Multi-Page External Dashboard Embedding: DataGOL now supports embedding multiple dashboard pages from a workspace together via the External Dashboard option. Previously, only a single dashboard page could be embedded at a time. With this update, you can bundle multiple pages into one external dashboard link, allowing end users to navigate between pages within the embedded view , just as they would inside DataGOL. This is ideal for client-facing portals or internal tools where users need access to several related dashboards without switching between separate embed links.
Date released: June 8, 2026

AgentOps Filters: AgentOps now supports filtering agent operations by request tags and model providers, enabling users to isolate and analyze specific agents, models, or workloads from within the operations dashboard.
Date released: June 4, 2026

Following improvements have been done for External Dashboards, improving the experience for users accessing dashboards across companies. Filter Support – Users can now successfully add and apply filters on shared External Dashboards. Show as Table – The Show as Table option now correctly displays widget data in a tabular format. Widget Data Download – Downloading widget data from shared External Dashboards now works as expected.
Date released: June 8, 2026

More model choice with OpenRouter You can now use OpenRouter to access open-source models like DeepSeek and Qwen. This gives your team more flexibility to choose the right model for different use cases, costs, and performance needs. Better visibility into Custom Agent usage: Custom Agent Analytics now shows the top users by tokens, requests, and cost. This makes it easier to understand usage patterns, monitor spend, and identify where to optimize agent activity. More charting and analysis in D.A.V.E: D.A.V.E. now handles chart creation and data analysis more reliably, with better support for advanced visuals like heatmaps and clearer handling of chart requirements such as sunburst views. These improvements help users get the right visualization faster and reduce errors when working with more complex requests.

Workbook Data Enrichment with DataBar AI Workbooks now support DataBar-powered enrichment, allowing you to enrich your data using providers like Google Maps, Diffbot, and People Data Labs directly within your workbook. Map inputs, select output fields, and run enrichments on individual rows, selected rows, or the full workbook.
Date released: June 11, 2026

Smarter tables and more dependable visualizations in D.A.V.E: D.A.V.E. now creates tables and charts more intelligently, with better default behavior for sorting, pinned columns, heatmaps, and data bars. This means users get clearer, more polished outputs automatically, even when they do not specify every formatting detail.

Resolved an issue where the Data Science Agent could appear stuck on “Thinking” and end with “Failed to send response,” even though the answer was generated successfully in the background. Responses now stream and render properly in the UI, so users can see results without needing to refresh the page.
Date released: June 12, 2026

Connect Custom Agents to Your Favorite Tools Configure and authenticate MCP connectors directly from the agent setup screen and assign them to your Custom Agents. Integrate with Google Workspace (Gmail, Calendar, Drive), Confluence, Jira, Fellow, PostHog, and many other supported platforms, allowing agents to retrieve and use information from your connected applications. MCP connectors are now private by default. Only the user who created a connector can see or modify it, giving each team member clear ownership over their own configurations and preventing accidental changes by others.

Fixed a navigation issue where clicking "Deny" during OAuth2.1 authorization for an MCP connector redirected users to the connector page instead of the Settings page. Users are now returned to the correct location. Resolved intermittent "unhandled errors" that occasionally appeared during conversations with Custom Agents.
Date released: June 15, 2026

D.A.V.E. Agent — Smarter, More Reliable Chart Rendering: D.A.V.E. now generates charts in a single step instead of two, eliminating an entire class of errors where data was fetched but never visualised, or the wrong dataset was charted. Conversations are also more consistent across long sessions and after resuming — agent rules now persist through compaction and session restores. Additional improvements include more reliable heatmap routing, cleaner table formatting with auto-frozen first columns on wide tables, and hardened handling of large query results that previously caused widget rendering failures. Skill Editing Restricted to Agent Owner: Only the owner or creator of a Custom Agent can now create, update, or delete its Skills. Users without ownership permissions will see a clear error message if they attempt to make changes, ensuring your agent's behavior stays under your control.

Timezone Localization Date Format Respects User Timezone:** Date and time formatting across the platform now automatically respects each user's configured timezone settings, ensuring information is displayed in their local time. Type-Ahead Search on Dashboard Parameters Dashboard parameter controls now include a search box, making it faster to find the right value in long lists without having to scroll through every option.

Resolved an issue where shared agents could use an incorrect default LLM model instead of the configured one. Shared agents now consistently use the selected model for all users, ensuring reliable and consistent AI responses. Fixed an issue where the Save button became hidden after adding new Allowed Hosts in the dashboard embedding configuration modal. Changes can now be saved without issue.
Date released: June 16, 2026

Scheduled Schema Sync: Your data sources now stay in sync automatically — no more discovering broken pipelines or broken charts after a schema change. The platform now runs schema synchronization twice daily, detecting new tables, added or removed columns, and data type changes, then updating metadata accordingly. Existing pipelines continue running uninterrupted for non-breaking changes, and sync logs are available for visibility into what changed and when.

"Has Any Of" Join Condition for Dynamic Workbooks: A new join operator — Has Any Of — is now available when linking two Dynamic Workbooks. It lets you match a single value against a delimiter-separated list stored in another column (for example, matching "Jane Smith" against "John Doe, Jane Smith, Bob Lee"). The delimiter is configurable, and whitespace around each value is trimmed automatically, making it easy to join on multi-value text fields without any custom SQL.
Date released: June 22, 2026

Lakehouse Access Control for New Users: Admins can now configure whether newly created users automatically get access to the Lakehouse layer. When restricted, the Lakehouse section is hidden from the user's view and the "Add Datasource" step is removed from the onboarding flow — keeping new users focused on the right experience from day one. The setting is available as a company-level toggle in Admin Platform configuration and applies to users created through both workspace invitations and direct registration. Gemini Models Now Available via OpenRouter: Gemini models are now accessible through OpenRouter, expanding the selection of AI models available for your agents and company configuration. Improved AI Request Traceability: Message IDs are now included in LiteLLM request tags and context, making it easier to trace, debug, and audit AI model requests across your environment.
Date released: June 23, 2026

Audio & Video Files Now Supported in Workspace Documents You can now upload .mp3 and .mp4 files to Workspace Documents and query their contents just like any other document. Audio files are transcribed automatically, and video files have their audio extracted and transcribed — all using the Whisper speech-to-text model. The resulting transcripts are chunked, embedded, and indexed for semantic search, so you can ask natural language questions against meetings, recordings, and any spoken content in your workspace.
Date released: June 24, 2026

More Reliable Long-Running Agent Tasks: Long-running agent tasks no longer drop connections mid-execution. Heartbeat responses are now sent during extended operations, keeping the connection alive and ensuring results are delivered reliably even when tasks take significant time to complete. Under the Hood: AI Service Improvements: This release includes internal platform improvements that make the AI service faster to maintain and more consistent across all agent types.
Date released: June 18, 2026

Granular MCP Tool Permissions for Custom Agents Admins can now control exactly which tools a Custom Agent is allowed to use from each connected MCP connector. Individual tools — such as sending emails, creating Jira issues, or uploading files — can be toggled on or off directly from the agent configuration UI. Changes take effect immediately on the next user message with no server restart required. This makes it easy to restrict agents to read-only operations, block destructive actions, or enforce compliance boundaries across any combination of connected services. Together AI Models Now Available: Together AI models can now be selected in company configuration and assigned to Custom Agents, expanding the range of LLM options available across your organization.

Resolved an issue where page-level filters were taking precedence over drill-down selections, causing drill-down to return incorrect results. Drill-down filters now apply correctly regardless of existing page filters. Fixed an issue where drilling down on high-cardinality dimensions such as Name, Email ID, or User ID returned empty results even when matching records existed. Drill-down now works correctly across all field types. Fixed a bug where renaming a chart label caused drill-down queries to fail. Drill-down now correctly uses the underlying data value for filtering while still displaying the updated label in the UI. Resolved two bugs in widget Explore Mode — a duplicate value field that appeared when entering filter values, and Equals / Includes / Contains filters not working as expected. All filter types in Explore Mode now behave correctly. Fixed a formatting issue where downloading a Pivot Table as CSV produced misaligned columns with data split across multiple cells. Exported CSV files now accurately reflect the pivot table structure. Resolved an issue where a widget's configured Help Message was erased whenever the widget was updated. Help Messages now persist through edits unless explicitly removed. Fixed an issue where the copy icon on the Embed Dashboard Configuration page did not copy the code snippet to the clipboard. Clicking the copy icon now works as expected.
Date released: June 24, 2026

Bulk Operations for Workbook & Workspace MCPs: MCP tools for workbooks and workspaces now support bulk create and bulk update operations, making it possible to manage large numbers of records in a single call. Each item in a bulk request is individually validated, and errors are surfaced per-item without blocking the rest of the batch. Column creation via workbook MCP has also been fixed to ensure new columns are always created with the correct name, type, and position.

Smarter Formula Columns in Dynamic Workbooks: Formula columns that reference lookup columns are now calculated dynamically at runtime instead of being stored in the database. Formulas that do not reference any lookup columns continue to be stored as before. This ensures your computed values always stay accurate as linked data changes, without any extra manual refresh.
Date released: June 30, 2026

Agent Scheduling: Custom Agents can now be scheduled to run automatically. Each scheduled execution creates its own conversation, runs the agent via a managed workflow, and records the outcome — including status (Running, Completed, or Failed) and any error details. A paginated API is available to list and filter run history per agent.
Resolved an issue with incorrect date handling in the SFTP connector that could cause data to load with wrong date values.
Date released: July 2, 2026

More Reliable Sign-Up & OTP Verification: OTPs for sign-up and MFA flows are now stored in the database instead of the Redis cache, eliminating verification failures that occurred when the cache was restarted during an active session. The registration event flow has also been made fully asynchronous for improved reliability. New company registrations now automatically provision default whitelisted data sources, removing the need for manual setup after sign-up.

Pipeline List Loads Faster: The get-all pipelines query has been optimised to batch-fetch workbook and workspace details in a single query instead of making individual database calls per pipeline. This eliminates an N+1 query pattern and significantly improves load times for accounts with many pipelines.
Date released: July 2, 2026

Human-in-the-Loop Approval for MCP Tool Execution: Admins can now configure individual MCP tools to require user approval before the agent executes them — a new NEEDS_APPROVAL permission level sits between ALLOW and BLOCKED. When a tool requires approval, the agent pauses and presents the user with the proposed action and its parameters. The user can approve (execute as-is), reject (cancel cleanly), modify parameters (agent re-calls with updated args and triggers a new approval), or ask a completely different question (pending approval is silently skipped). Changes take effect immediately with no server restart needed.

Improved the dynamic parameter experience on dashboards: Parameter width is now wider, selected values appear at the top of the list for quick visibility, and label rendering issues for single-value dynamic parameters have been fixed. Folder Structure & Filter for Dashboard Navigation A folder-based structure with breadcrumb navigation and a folder filter is now available in the dashboard browser, making it easier to organise and locate dashboards across large collections.

Fixed an issue where Drill Down V3 on draft widgets ignored any widget-level filters configured on the source widget. Drill-down results now correctly inherit and apply all widget-level filters. Resolved an issue where page-level filters took precedence over drill-down selections on widgets. Drill-down filters now apply correctly.
Date released: July 6, 2026

Skill Deletion Warning When Agents Are Affected: Deleting a Skill that is used by one or more Custom Agents now shows a warning modal before proceeding. The modal lists how many agents are affected, names each one, and lets you open them in a new tab for review — so you can make an informed decision before removing a Skill that others depend on. This protection is consistent whether you delete from the Agent Builder or the Skills library.
Date released: July 7, 2026

Databar Enrichment — Selected Output Columns: When configuring a Databar enrichment, you can now control exactly which output fields are written back to your workbook, giving you finer-grained control over which enriched data columns are created.

Resolved a bug where uni-directional BelongsTo and reverse HasMany workbook link operations failed silently due to an incorrect source column ID being stored. Linking, de-linking, and retrieving linked records now works correctly across all relationship types. Fixed an issue where agents querying warehouse-backed workbooks (BigQuery, Snowflake, Athena, Redshift, MySQL, SQL Server) always defaulted to Spark SQL instead of generating queries in the correct dialect. Each engine now receives properly targeted SQL.
Date released: July 8, 2026

Auto Join — Optional Whitespace Trimming​ A new "Trim white space" option is now available on each Auto Join condition. Enabled by default, it trims leading and trailing whitespace from values before comparison — preserving the existing behaviour. You can disable it per condition when exact-match comparison (including whitespace) is needed. The setting takes effect only after saving the Auto Join configuration; existing joins are not automatically changed. Email Column Improvements​ Two improvements to Email columns in workbooks: Comma-separated emails now display correctly — cells containing multiple email addresses separated by commas are parsed and rendered cleanly, with no overlap or broken display. Email columns can now be mapped during Append/Replace — a mismatch between backend storage types (VARCHAR(255) vs TEXT) previously prevented Email columns from appearing as mapping options. The mapping now compares logical column types, so Email-to-Email mapping works as expected.
Date released: July 10, 2026

D.A.V.E. Now Supports Analysis Across Multiple Workbooks: You can now select two or more workbooks in a single D.A.V.E. conversation and ask questions across all of them at once, instead of being limited to one workbook per session. This makes it easier to compare, combine, and analyze data that lives in different workbooks without starting a separate conversation for each one.
Date released: July 14, 2026

Stop Button Now Reliably Cancels Streaming Agent Responses: Fixed an issue where pressing Stop had no effect after a page refresh while an agent was still generating a response. The agent now stops immediately, even when the stream was restored across a refresh.

Inline Record Linking from Expanded View: You can now create and link new records directly from the expanded row view without leaving your current context. Whether adding a linked record that doesn't exist yet or editing an existing one, everything happens inline — no more navigating away, creating the record elsewhere, and finding your way back. Link and Lookup Columns Included in Workbook Exports: Workbook downloads now include link and lookup columns, so what you export matches exactly what you see on screen. Previously these columns were silently excluded, leaving gaps in downloaded files.
Date released: July 15, 2026

Fireflies & Granola Data Source Connectors: You can now connect Fireflies and Granola as data sources to automatically sync meeting transcripts and notes into your pipelines — no more manual exports. Both connectors support incremental sync and are available under Data Sources.

Updated Field-Type Icons (Abc / # / Globe): Field icons in the Tables panel, chart builder, and filters now use industry-standard conventions: Abc for text fields, # for numeric fields, and a globe icon for geographic fields. This makes workbook schemas faster to scan for users familiar with Tableau or Looker.
Resolved an issue where scheduled Custom Agent executions were failing to run and not producing any output thread. Agents now execute reliably at their configured schedule time.
Date released: July 21, 2026

Confluence Connector for Knowledge Base: You can now connect Confluence as a Knowledge Base source. Sync entire spaces or individual page URLs, and your AI agents will be able to search and answer questions against indexed content. Full and incremental syncs are supported.

Fathom Data Source Connector: Fathom is now available as a data source, letting you sync meeting recordings, transcripts, summaries, and action items directly into your pipelines via API key — consistent with the existing Granola and Fireflies integrations.
Date released: July 21, 2026

Skill Management Experience Improved: Creating, editing, and importing Custom Agent skills is now smoother: skill names are auto-formatted to meet naming conventions, duplicate names trigger a rename suggestion, and you'll be prompted to save unsaved changes before navigating away.

Resolved an error that caused Custom Agents configured with many MCP integrations to fail entirely due to exceeding the model's 128-tool limit. A smart tool-selector now activates automatically when needed, routing each query to the most relevant tools — without adding latency for smaller configurations.
Date released: July 17, 2026

D.A.V.E. Improvements for Custom Agents: Custom Agents backed by large workbooks (1,000+ records) now automatically route SQL queries through D.A.V.E., ensuring more accurate results at scale. Query responses return only data and analysis — no unwanted charts or widgets generated alongside.

Static ↔ Dynamic Workbook Linking: Link columns can now connect static and dynamic workbooks in both directions. Previously only dynamic-to-dynamic and dynamic-to-hybrid links were supported, requiring workarounds for common reference-data relationships.

Enhanced PDF Export for BI Dashboards: The Print/Export PDF functionality for dashboards has been enhanced with better formatting, improved layout consistency, and more reliable output across different dashboard configurations.
Resolved several issues affecting the behavior and reliability of custom skills within D.A.V.E.-powered agents.
Date released: July 24, 2026

Row Limit Option for Table Widgets: Dashboard table widgets now support an optional row limit setting, letting you cap the number of rows displayed at creation time. This improves performance for large datasets while keeping drill-down into historical data available. Cohort Widget Enhancements: Formula columns in cohort widgets now support percentage formatting, and percentage-based metrics are aggregated correctly. Drill-down from weekly retention metrics is also now available, showing exactly which users returned or churned in any given week.

Custom Agent: Smarter Workbook & Tool Routing: Custom Agents now include a workbook catalog in their system context, enabling accurate cross-workbook routing and preventing unnecessary fan-out to unrelated tools. D.A.V.E. sub-agents now run on the same model selected for the parent agent and no longer restate answers already streamed to the user.

Resolved several issues with page-level and linked filters: the Reset button now correctly restores defaults, Apply works on the first click, the Include operator no longer switches to Equal unexpectedly, and linked filters correctly surface values from the configured base workbook. Fixed an issue where drilling down on a widget grouped by weekly date applied the date range in reverse order, returning no results. Drill-downs now use the correct chronological start-to-end date range. Date columns with NULL values now display as blank instead of showing the Unix epoch date 1970-01-01. Resolved an issue where the Show as Table option displayed incorrect column names and inaccurate cumulative count values.
Date released: July 28, 2026

Skill Version History: Custom Agent skills now maintain a full version history. Every save creates a new version, and you can view the complete timeline, download any previous version, or recover from a bad update without losing earlier configurations. Smarter Workbook Indexing for AI Knowledge Base: Column descriptions are now included when indexing workbooks into the Knowledge Base, giving the AI richer context for more accurate answers. Cell values are also trimmed of extra whitespace before indexing for cleaner embeddings.
Date released: July 30, 2026

Gmail & Google Calendar Datasources: One-Click OAuth: Adding Gmail or Google Calendar as a data source no longer requires manually entering OAuth credentials. A Connect button now opens the same authorization flow used on the Connectors page — authorize once and you're done.

Comments Indicator Always Visible on Workbook Rows: Rows with existing comments now display a persistent indicator by default, so you can spot commented rows at a glance without hovering over each one. Self-Referencing Link Columns Within a Workbook: Link columns now support referencing records within the same workbook, enabling hierarchical relationships like tasks and subtasks, parent and child records, or organizational hierarchies — all within a single workbook.

Fixed an issue where opening a workspace briefly showed "Workspace unavailable" while the workspace list finished loading. The current workspace now resolves immediately and appears in the header without the delay. Fixed a crash on the Data Sources page when a connection had no name. The page now loads normally and displays a fallback label for unnamed connections. Significantly reduced load times for the pipelines page on large accounts. Redundant data was removed from API responses and N+1 database query patterns were replaced with batched lookups, cutting latency substantially.
Date released: July 31, 2026

Google Ads Connector: You can now connect Google Ads as a data source and sync campaign performance data directly into workbooks — no more manual CSV exports. Full ETL support enables automated, repeatable performance marketing analytics on ad spend and campaign performance. Deduplication Pipeline: APPEND Mode for Iceberg: The deduplication pipeline now supports APPEND writes for Iceberg warehouse tables, enabling incremental ingestion without introducing duplicate records.

Historical Data Downloads from Dashboards: You can now download historical data directly from dashboard widgets, pulling from the data warehouse rather than the workbook layer. This removes the prior retention limitation, supports large date ranges, and delivers results asynchronously via a secure email link in CSV format.

Resolved three security issues identified during a backend audit: two internal endpoints that skipped token validation now correctly enforce it, and data source credentials are now always masked in API responses regardless of query parameters. No user-facing flows or API contracts were changed. Resolved an error causing dashboards with multiple widgets backed by the same BigQuery table to fail with "too many table update operations." The platform now checks whether an external table exists using a metadata read rather than a DDL operation, avoiding BigQuery's rate limit entirely. Third-party embedded dashboards now support table data downloads scoped to tenant filters and caller-supplied conditions. Requests are handled asynchronously and results are delivered to the requester's email as a secure CSV link. Data source names are now checked for uniqueness across all tenants at creation time, preventing naming conflicts at the storage layer. Existing sources and system-created sources are unaffected. Resolved several reliability issues: upstream failures no longer appear as assistant messages, authentication now works correctly for cookie-only sessions and after token refresh, and cached agent instances no longer use expired tokens across requests.
Date released: July 9, 2026

Long-Term Memory for Custom Agents: Custom Agents now have access to a search_memory tool powered by mem0, enabling retrieval of stored memories across three scopes: user-level, company-level, and agent-level. The agent proactively applies relevant memories — such as preferred output formats, response style, or domain rules — to improve the quality and consistency of its responses across conversations. Memory Search Scope Isolation Fixed: search results were not being filtered by scope (allowing cross-user memory leakage), agent ID updates were not persisted on memory records, and scope transitions (e.g., user → company) failed silently. All three are now fixed — memory search is fully isolated by scope, updates persist correctly, and scope transitions perform a proper delete-and-recreate. Agent UI & UX Fixes​ Several usability improvements to the Agents page: The message input box no longer disappears when switching between active threads. Citation cards no longer overflow when the citation description is long. Opening Knowledge Source links from the Agent Builder no longer triggers an unwanted "Leave page?" confirmation dialog. The Generated Files/Datasets section has been redesigned with a clearer, more clickable layout.
Date released: August 3, 2026

D.A.V.E. Charts & Widgets Now Render Inside Custom Agents: When D.A.V.E. is invoked from a Custom Agent with workbooks connected via MCP, charts and data tables now render directly in the agent response — the same way they do in a standalone D.A.V.E. session. You can pin those visualizations straight to a dashboard without leaving the conversation. Download Skills from the Skill Page: Skills can now be downloaded directly from the skill page as a plain-text file, named using the standard DataGOL convention. You can save any skill locally for reference, reuse, or offline access without copying content manually. Featured Agents Now Available in Analytics Filters: The Agent Cost and Trace analytics pages now include Featured Agents — such as D.A.V.E. — alongside Custom Agents in the filter options. You can analyze usage, costs, and execution traces across every agent type from a single view.

Self-Referencing Link Columns in Workbooks: You can now create link columns that point back to the same workbook, making it easy to model hierarchical relationships — such as tasks and subtasks, parent and child records, or org chart reporting lines — without needing a separate workbook or manual workarounds.

Seamless Navigation Between DataGOL and Apps: Apps now open directly within the DataGOL platform, so the experience feels native rather than disconnected. A lightweight DataGOL header slides in when you hover near the top of the screen, giving you a quick way to return to the main application without disrupting your workspace. Secure Token Passing for Embedded Apps: Embedded Apps now receive the authenticated DataGOL session token automatically from the parent window, using a standardized and secure script that is included in every generated App. Individual Apps no longer need to implement their own authentication logic, keeping behavior consistent and reducing setup effort.

Resolved several issues with link and lookup columns: lookup values no longer persist after the source record is deleted; expanded lookup views now display values correctly; creating an auto-join link column no longer throws a duplicate table error; and adding multiple records to a many-to-one link column no longer returns a bad request error. Fixed an issue where publishing a No-Copy Postgres workbook containing a JSON or JSONB column caused the UI to break after publish. Affected workbooks now display correctly.
Date released: August 5, 2026

OCR Support for Scanned PDFs in File Upload: Custom Agents can now extract and index text from scanned or faxed PDFs that contain no text layer. Pages without readable text are automatically processed using OCR, so your agent can reference the full content of image-based documents — not just digitally created ones.

Multi-Select Filter Operators Redesigned: Filtering on multi-select columns is now accurate and intuitive. The old Contains and Does Not Contain operators — which incorrectly matched values as a combined string — have been replaced with Has Any Of, Has None Of, and a new Is Exactly operator. Each selected option is now evaluated independently, so filters return the right records regardless of value order or how many options a cell contains.

App Version History (AppX): AppX now tracks version history for published applications, giving teams visibility into what changed across releases and the ability to reference or recover earlier versions when needed.

Fixed a high-priority bug where applying a multi-select filter on a JDBC-backed workbook caused a 400 Bad Request error, making the filtered view completely unusable. Filtered views now load correctly.
Date released: August 10, 2026

Workbook Agent: A dedicated Workbook Agent is now available, enabling natural-language interaction directly with your workbook data for a faster, more intuitive way to explore and act on your information. OrchX: OrchX is now available, bringing orchestration capabilities to coordinate complex, multi-step workflows across your data and agents.

Fixed an issue where attached files were invisible to the agent — the model would report that no file was provided even when one had been uploaded. Attachments are now surfaced correctly in the agent's context, and the tools that read attached files work as expected.
Date released: August 11, 2026

Agent & Thread Navigation Redesigned for Scale: Finding the right agent or conversation is now faster and easier. Thread timestamps are visible at a glance without hovering, pinned agents take up less space with a more compact layout, and starting a new chat requires fewer clicks. Navigation behavior is now consistent across Featured and Custom Agents throughout the platform. Per-Agent Disclaimer Messages: Admins can now configure a custom disclaimer message for each agent, displayed above "Powered by DataGOL" in the chat. When no custom message is set, a sensible default is shown. Toggle the disclaimer on or off per agent — changes to one agent never affect any other. Featured Agent Settings Aligned with Custom Agent Builder: The settings page for Featured Agents now matches the design and layout of the Custom Agent Builder, creating a consistent configuration experience across all agent types.
Date released: August 11, 2026

Scheduled PDF Delivery for Dashboards You can now schedule automated PDF delivery of a dashboard or individual widget to your email on a recurring basis. Configure the recipient list, frequency, delivery time, and relative date range — such as "last 7 days" — and DataGOL will generate and send the report automatically at the scheduled time. Faster BigQuery Queries via Result Caching: BigQuery's built-in result cache is now fully utilized. Previously, query names were randomly generated on every request, making each query appear unique even when the filters and parameters were identical. Queries are now generated deterministically, so repeated requests return cached results faster and at lower cost.

Access & Refresh Token Authentication: Session authentication now uses short-lived access tokens paired with long-lived refresh tokens, enabling explicit server-side logout and seamless token renewal without requiring users to re-authenticate. This satisfies client requirements for token validation and session control.
Date released: August 12, 2026

D.A.V.E. Now Queries All Workspaces Bound to an Agent: When a Custom Agent has workbooks from multiple workspaces, D.A.V.E. now queries all of them — not just the first one it found. Previously, workbooks from additional workspaces were silently dropped, causing the agent to fail or return incomplete answers. All connected workbooks are now reachable. Long-Running D.A.V.E. Queries No Longer Time Out Prematurely: D.A.V.E. queries that take a long time to execute — such as those running large Spark jobs — no longer get cut off by a fixed 15-minute wall-clock deadline. The timeout is now activity-based, so queries are only terminated when there is genuine silence from the upstream, not just because they are taking time.

Fixed an issue where D.A.V.E. failures — such as timeouts or upstream errors — were returned as ordinary assistant text and treated as successful responses. Errors are now correctly flagged, shown to the user with a friendly message, and never folded into the agent's analysis as if they were data. Fixed an issue where HTML content returned by a Custom Agent took up far more vertical space than the actual content, leaving large blank areas in the chat. The HTML container now sizes itself to fit its content, with scrolling available for very large responses. Resolved synchronization issues with the Projects sidebar in AppX, ensuring the navigation state stays consistent and up to date.
Date released: August 13, 2026

Document Processing Jobs Now Run via Queue: Parsing, classification, and extraction workflows for documents are now processed through a managed jobs queue with heartbeat monitoring and deterministic workflow IDs. Stuck jobs are detected and terminated within minutes rather than running indefinitely, and duplicate processing on retry is prevented automatically.

Fixed an issue where agents with many MCP tools connected could silently lose access to workbook write operations — such as adding or updating rows — due to tool selection pruning. Write tools are now always available, and for agents connected to many workbooks, the available write capacity is distributed fairly rather than front-loaded. Fixed a high-priority issue where creating a page-level filter on a dashboard resulted in a blank filter name and the filter not appearing on the dashboard at all. Filters now save and display correctly after configuration. Fixed an issue where the Python Agent failed on ETL workbooks (MV + Last Mile) because it was still pointing to the old S3 storage location after the GCP migration. The agent now reads Parquet files from GCS correctly using per-company storage keys. Fixed a race condition where completing a warehouse pipeline could leave a brief window during which concurrent pipelines reading from the same BigQuery table would fail with a "table not found" error. The external table is now recreated immediately after being dropped, closing that gap.

Workbooks provide a versatile solution, empowering you to organize, analyze, and visualize your data with ease. Whether you are building dynamic reports or managing critical datasets, understanding the capabilities of workbooks is key to unlocking your data's full potential. Workbooks provide a robust and flexible framework for managing your data lifecycle. From static, automatically updated datasets to dynamic, fully customizable workbooks, coupled with intelligent features and granular access control, this platform empowers you to effectively organize, analyze, and visualize your information, driving informed decisions and unlocking valuable insights. Workbooks also enable the creation of formulas, allowing for the generation of distinct subviews tailored for insightful data visualization. Your workspace serves as the central hub for your workbooks. These workbooks can be created in the following ways: Manual create blank workbook Published from Playground File upload (Excel or CSV) There are two types of workbooks in DataGOL: Static Workbooks (Non-Editable): These workbooks function as dynamic representations of your data. Powered by a data source, they automatically update to reflect the latest information, ensuring your insights are always current. A lock icon clearly identifies these workbooks, signifying their data source-driven nature and non-editable by users. Dynamic Workbooks (Editable): These workbooks are either created manually or uploaded from a file and can be edited with the appropriate permissions. You can customize them to your specific needs by adding new columns, applying filters, and incorporating powerful formulas. [NOTE] Static workbooks now exclusively use Spark functions, while dynamic workbooks utilize JDBC functions.

Your valuable work in workbooks can be safeguarded with delete protection, a built-in feature. This acts as a crucial safeguard, preventing accidental deletions, especially for workbooks integral to reports, dashboards, or other critical workflows. Importantly, admin control ensures that only authorized users can enable or disable this protection.
Group workbooks in folders by shared attributes for better organization and faster access.

To enrich your data and tailor it to your specific needs, workbooks support a diverse range of column types: Single Line Text: For concise text entries. Long Text: Ideal for detailed notes, HTML markups, and rich text. Checkbox: A simple toggle for binary status tracking. Multi-Select: Enables the selection of multiple options from a predefined list. You have the option to auto-generate the options based on values in a column. It's recommended to keep the number of options to 8K. You can provide a display name for each option if data is stored as enum. Single Select: Allows choosing one option from a predefined list. You have the option to auto-generate the options based on values in a column. It's recommended to keep the number of options to 8K. You can provide a display name for each option if data is stored as enum. Date: For storing and selecting dates with an intuitive calendar. Date Column Phone Number: Dedicated input for telephone numbers. Email: Specifically designed for storing email addresses. URL: For entering and validating website links. Number: Stores numeric values, including both integers and decimals. Currency: Formats numbers as monetary values in various currencies (USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CHF, INR). Currency column Percentage: Displays numerical values as percentages. Formula: Calculates values dynamically based on defined expressions. Attachment: Facilitates file uploads with previews for common image and document formats. Link / Lookup: Enables referencing values from other workbooks, fostering relationships between datasets. User: Allows you to add or tag one or multiple users to a specific row. Button: Allows you to push a record to a different workbook or generate Jira tickets directly from a workbook, supporting both individual and bulk issue creation.

Data entry is streamlined through an intuitive form view, accessible by expanding any row. This feature provides a structured input interface, making it easier to manage large forms and ensuring enhanced readability for users entering multiple details per record without the need for extensive scrolling. Refer to Viewing and editing details of a row in a form.

All the permissions in a workbook are inherited from the workspace. The following permissions are inherited: Invite Users: Allows you to bring collaborators into your workspace, regardless of their organization. Viewer: Can apply filters and create personalized views but cannot modify the workbook's content. Editor: Possesses all Viewer permissions and can edit dynamic workbooks. Creator: Holds comprehensive control, including Editor permissions, managing settings, enabling delete protection, configuring workbook permissions, and controlling sharing options.

On the Home page, from the left navigation panel, click Workspace, and from the list of workspaces, open the workspace where the workbook that you want to edit is located. Click the Workbook tab and select the required workbook. Click the Settings button on the top and select View pipeline. The pipeline information is displayed. You can readily view the underlying query driving this workbook, an option available for workbooks connected to a data source. To modify the query, navigate to the pipeline and edit the corresponding stream. If this workbook was published directly from the Playground without creating a copy, you'll have the convenience of editing the query directly from the panel within the workbook itself. You can view the freshness of your data here, along with the status of the Last Mile Pipeline, which handles the final step of moving data from S3 storage into DB storage—converting it into a more accessible format for querying and analysis.

You can append new data to existing workbooks or replace entire sheets with revised data. If you need to do any of the following, then appending the workbook with the required data or replacing the entire workbook is a good solution: Periodic data updates: You can upload monthly, weekly, or daily exports and append them to existing data. Bulk corrections: You can clean and reformat data offline, then replace the entire workbook. Dashboard & Pipeline continuity: When a workbook is used in dashboards or materialized view (MV) pipelines, replacing the data avoids the need to change the workbook reference. This allows you to refresh the full dataset without breaking downstream connections or reconfiguring linked components. Note This functionality is not available for static tables. To append or replace data in a workbook, do the following: In a workbook, click Settings from the top and select Import Data. In the Import dialog box, specify the type of file you want to upload and upload the file. In the Import dialog box, specify whether you want to append or replace by clicking the corresponding buttons. Here, you can also modify the column mapping. Click Append/Replace.
documents.s: Append or replace data in workbooks

documents.t: Previously, importing data into a workbook with a lookup column only matched the first value in a cell — any additional comma-separated values were silently dropped, and if no exact match was found, the cell was left blank. With this enhancement, the system now splits imported cell values by comma and matches each one individually against the linked workbook, populating all matched entries into the lookup column in a single cell. The use case this solves: Consider you have a People workbook and a Projects workbook where Projects has a lookup column linked to People. When you import a CSV into Projects where a cell contains multiple names (e.g. John Doe, Alice, Mark), the system now resolves each name against the People workbook and populates all matched entries — instead of only the first match. How to use it: Set up a workbook with a link column pointing to another workbook (e.g. Projects → People). Go to Settings → Append and upload your import file. Map the import column to the lookup field and select the matching column in the linked workbook. On import, any comma-separated values in that column are each matched individually against the linked workbook. All matched entries are populated into the lookup cell — supporting one-to-many matches in a single row. What stays the same: The lookup column type remains a string/text field — it is not converted to multi-select. Existing formulas and lookups built on top of this column continue to work as before. Known limitations: Applies to data imported via the Append workflow — not to manual row entry. Only values that find an exact match in the linked workbook are populated; unmatched values are skipped.
documents.s: Links & Joins — Comma-Separated Multi-Value Matching on Import

documents.t: To edit the name and description of a workbook, do the following: On the Home page, from the left navigation panel, click Workspace, and from the list of workspaces, open the workspace where the workbook that you want to edit is located. Click the Workbook tab and select the workbook that you want to edit. Click the Settings button on the top and select Edit Name and Description. Edit the name and description of the workbook, and then click Save.
documents.s: Editing name and description of a workbook

documents.t: The Column Extraction feature enables you to automatically extract structured data fields from unstructured sources — such as meeting transcripts, recorded calls, or text documents — using an AI agent. Rather than manually reviewing lengthy content, you can configure an extraction pipeline that pulls specific fields into a structured workbook with minimal effort.

When unstructured records (e.g., meeting transcripts) are imported into a workbook, the extraction feature allows you to define the fields you want to capture, preview the results, save the configuration for reuse, and run the extraction across multiple records simultaneously.

Before using Column Extraction, ensure the following: Your source data (e.g., transcripts) has been imported into a workbook either through import or query. You have at least one record available to extract from. You have access to an existing destination workbook, or you are prepared to create a new one.

Open your workbook containing the source records. Select the record(s) you wish to extract from. Click the Extract option from the dropdown menu on the column toolbar. The extraction panel will open, displaying the selected source record on the left and configuration options on the right.

In the extraction panel, select where the extracted data should be written: Option Description Create a New Workbook Generates a new workbook with columns based on the fields you define. Use an Existing Workbook Maps extracted fields to columns that already exist in a chosen workbook.

Enter a descriptive name for this extraction configuration (e.g., Financial Extraction). Note: Naming the extraction is important. Saved extractions can be reused when new records are added, eliminating the need to reconfigure from scratch each time.

Choose the mode that best fits the structure of the data you need to extract: Mode Best For Standard Simple, flat fields — such as names, numbers, or single values. Advanced Nested objects, complex structures, or data requiring a specific output format.

In the prompt input, describe the fields you want the AI agent to extract. For example: Extract: NRR, gross margin percentage, burn rate, fundraising amount, and lifetime value. Click Generate. The agent will process the prompt and prepare the corresponding extraction fields automatically. Adding Fields Manually​ After generation, you can add additional fields at any time: Click Add a Field. Provide a column name for the new field. Enter a description to instruct the agent on what to extract. If using an existing workbook, map the field to an existing column.
documents.s: Step 5: Define the Fields to Extract

documents.t: Select the column to use as the primary key for the destination workbook (e.g., an ID column). This uniquely identifies each extracted record.

Before saving and running an extraction, you can validate the output: Click Preview Results. The agent will run the extraction on the currently selected record only. Review the extracted values in the preview panel to confirm all fields are populating correctly. Tip: Always preview your extraction on at least one representative record before saving the configuration, especially when working with advanced mode or nested fields.

Once the fields and settings are verified: Confirm or update the configuration name. Choose whether to store extracted data as JSON in addition to structured columns. Enabling this option preserves the raw AI response alongside the structured output. This is useful if you need to audit or reprocess responses at a later time. Click Create to save the extraction configuration.

After saving, the extraction is ready to execute: Click Run. Select the records you wish to process. Review the processing option: Process New Cells Only (enabled by default) — Skips records that have already been extracted, preventing duplicate processing. Click Run Extraction to begin. A progress screen will display the status of the extraction job. Once complete, a success notification will appear in the top-right corner of the interface.
Upon completion: Click View in the success notification. The destination workbook will open, displaying all extracted fields as structured columns across your records.

Saved extraction configurations are stored and accessible for future use. When new records or transcripts are added to your source workbook: Navigate to the saved extraction configuration. Click Run. Select the new records (or use Process New Cells Only to auto-filter). Run the extraction — no reconfiguration required.

The Column Catalog maps each workbook column to its corresponding source column from connected data sources. Any metadata cataloged at the data source level is automatically surfaced at the workbook column. If a column is derived from multiple sources, descriptions from each level will be shown. Its primary purpose is to help users trace the raw source and inherit cataloging information. On the Home page, from the left navigation panel, click Workspace, and from the list of workspaces, open the workspace where the workbook that you want to edit is located. Click the Workbook tab and select the required workbook. Click the Settings button on the top and select Column catalog. The column information is displayed. Optionally, you can turn on the Edit toggle to edit the column details. Click Save.
documents.s: Viewing and editing the column catalog in workbook

documents.t: To view the workbook information, do the following: On the Home page, from the left navigation panel, click Workspace, and from the list of workspaces, open the workspace where the workbook that you want to edit is located. Click the Workbook tab and select the required workbook. Click the Settings button on the top and select Workbook info. info Grid View is the main screen in the workbook, showing all the columns and your complete data in a table format. It gives you a full overview. Subview: This is a focused part of the main grid view. You create it by filtering the data to see only specific information. For example, in a list of all sales, a subview could show only the sales from the last quarter. The grid view is the whole table, and a subview is like zooming in on a specific section of that table to look closer at certain data. This helps you analyze specific parts of your data more easily.

You can copy the cURL command to interact with the workbook using API requests. This command includes the necessary method, headers, and parameters for easy integration. [NOTE] This cURL does not incorporate filters, sort conditions, or other view-specific properties. To include such properties, copy the cURL command available for the specific view. On the Home page, from the left navigation panel, click Workspace, and from the list of workspaces, open the workspace where the workbook that you want to edit is located. Click the Workbook tab and select the required workbook. Click the Settings button on the top and select Copy as cURL. The Copy cURL box is displayed with the cURL command. Click the copy icon to copy the cURL command.
documents.s: Copying cURL for workbook API interaction

documents.t: If you want to connect to specific records from another workbook in DataGOL, you create a Link. A Link is a direct relationship created between two different tables or workbooks. This is done by adding a specific column to a workbook and then manually or automatically connecting it to records in another workbook. Links are about connecting records and viewing related data within an existing workbook. They add a column to your current table. A Join combines data from two or more tables into a single, new workbook based on a specified condition. Joins are about combining entire workbooks to create a new, single workbook. They are a more permanent way to merge datasets for analysis or reporting.
documents.s: Creating links and joins in dynamic tables

documents.t: Links are used to visually connect records and see related data directly within a single table. They are useful for establishing a one-to-one or one-to-many relationship. 1. Create a new Link column In your parent workbook, create a new column. Select "Link" as the column type. 2. Configure the Link column Select Child Workbook: Choose the workbook you want to link to. Specify Join Type: Select a mapping type, such as one-to-one, one-to-many, or many-to-many. Choose Auto Join (Optional): Manual: You can manually link records by clicking the plus (+) button in the link column and selecting the specific record from the child table you want to connect to. This is ideal when there is no clear joining condition or if you need to be very specific about the connections. Automatic: Set a condition for the link to be created automatically. For example, if you set the condition as "Parent Table.ID equals Child Table.ID," the records will link themselves whenever their IDs match. Click Save. (Optional) From the Lookup box, select specific fields from the linked workbook to add them as Lookup fields in current workbook. 3. Select or add Lookups with Links Go to the Link column you just created. Click + sign and choose the specific field from the child workbook that you want to link. The value from the linked record will then appear in this new column. 4. View the linked recordss To view each linked record, you can expand the option in the parent workbook where the link was created. When you create a link, a new column is added to the parent workbook. Within this column, each cell represents a record. Click the expand button for a specific record, which reveals the values of the corresponding linked record(s) from the child workbook. Alternatively, you can create a lookup column. This method directly pulls and displays a specific field's value from the linked child record into a new column in your parent workbook. This allows you to see the mapped data without expanding the link for each record individually.

Joins are used to create a completely new workbook that combines data from multiple source workbooks. This results in a merged view of the data. Dynamic workbooks and workbooks that are converted from S3 to DB. You can create joins in the following types of workbooks: Dynamic workbooks Workbooks that are converted from S3 to DB Open the workbook from where you want to add Joins. From the Settings drop-down menu, select the Link Join Workbooks options. Configure the Join: In the Link / Join Workbooks box, select the Right Workbooks. The primary workbook you are working in is the "left" workbook, and the one you want to join to is the "right" workbook. This process typically performs a left outer join, meaning all records from the left workbook will be included, even if they don't have a matching record in the right workbook. Choose which columns from the joined workbooks you want to see in the new, combined workbook. This allows you to select only the relevant data. Specify the criteria for the join. For example, you might set the condition as "Left Workbook.ProductID equals Right Workbook.ProductID. Optionally, you can click Add a link to another workbook and add more Right workbooks. This method allows you to join multiple tables at once, creating complex combined datasets. Give the new workbook a name and click Create and Publish. The system will then generate a new workbook containing the joined data.
You can create a workbook in any of the following methods: Creating a blank workbook Creating a workbook from file upload (Excel or CSV) Publishing workbook from playground

To create a blank workbook, do the following: On the Home page, from the left navigation panel, click Workspace, and from the list of workspaces, open a workspace. From the left panel, at the bottom, click Create a Blank Workbook. A blank worksheet is created. You can add the desired columns and furnish the blank workbook with information.

On the Home page, from the left navigation panel, click Workspace, and from the list of workspaces, open a workspace. From the left panel, at the bottom, click Import. In the Import dialog box, do the following: Check the following settings if required: Use first record as headers Auto detect column types Specify the delimiter or the character that is used to separate the fields in the CSV file. Click Upload Excel or Upload CSV to upload the corresponding file from your system. A preview of the data you are importing is displayed. You can review the data and if there are any sheets you do not wish to import, you can close those tabs before proceeding. You can change the name or edit types from within the preview. You can upload Excel files with multiple sheets; each sheet will be imported as a workbook. Users have the option of removing some sheets from being imported from within the preview. Click Import. The import status is shown. Once the import is completed, you can click the Open button to open the Workbook. Optionally, you can also download this sheet.

Grouping workbook data against a chosen column offers a powerful way to reorganize and understand your information from different angles. Instead of just seeing a flat list of entries, you can create a hierarchical view where rows with the same value in your selected column are brought together. This aggregation allows you to analyze trends, summaries, and patterns specific to those groups. To ensure optimized performance, only datasets with less than 10,000 records is allowed for Data Grouping. Data Grouping allows you to dynamically organize your information based on a chosen common attribute, transforming lengthy lists into easily navigable, hierarchical structures. You can group up to three columns at a time. Grouping a column reveals summary rows for each group, making it easier to analyze patterns and totals within sections of the data. For numeric columns, the following aggregation options are supported: Average, Sum, Standard Variation, Range Minimum, Maximum, Median Count, Unique Count Most Frequent, Least Frequent Percent Filled, Percent Empty, Percent Unique For non-numeric columns, a limited set of aggregations is available: Most Frequent, Least Frequent Percent Filled, Percent Empty Percent Unique Once an aggregation is selected, it is automatically applied to each group under that column, allowing users to see consistent summaries at the group level. [NOTE] DataGOL recommends to group by columns that have distinct or categorical values (such as status, department, or region) to ensure meaningful groupings. For example, suppose your Sale Workbook has the following columns: Sales Region: (e.g., North, South, East, West) Sales: (the monetary value of each sale) Profits: (the profit margin for each sale) Transaction Date: (the date the sale occurred) Now, if you choose to group by Sales Region, the workbook's display would transform. Instead of showing individual sales records in a long list, you would see something like this: Sales Region Sales Profits Transaction dates North Region $XX,XXX $YY,YYY DD/MM/YY, DD/MM/YY Southern Region $AA,SS $BB,BBB DD/MM/YY, DD/MM/YY Western Region $CC,AA $CC,BBB DD/MM/YY, DD/MM/YY Eastern Region $DD,AA $CC,BBB DD/MM/YY, DD/MM/YY

On the Home page, from the left navigation panel, click Workspace and from the list of workspaces, open the workspace where the workbook that you want to edit is located. Click the Workbook tab and select the required workbook. Click the Group button from the top right. The Add group box is displayed. Select a column from the current workbook to group the data and click Save. The workbook data is now re-organized and grouped around the selected column.

[NOTE] Ensure that the workbook is not delete-protected before deleting it. If it is, you must first remove the delete protection status. Refer to Disable delete protection for workbooks for instructions. On the Home page, from the left navigation panel, click Workspace. From the list of workspaces, open the workspace containing the workbook you want to delete. Click the Workbook tab and select the desired workbook. Click the Settings button on the top and select Delete Workbook.

To disable delete protection for workbooks, do the following: On the Home page, from the left navigation panel, click Workspace, and from the list of workspaces, open the workspace where the workbook that you want to edit is located. Click the Workbook tab and select the required workbook. Click the Settings button on the top and select Set Delete Protection. In the Delete Protection Settings box, clear the Enable checkbox. Click Save.

There are two primary ways to download data from your workbooks, each with distinct behaviors: Downloading Raw Excel or CSV: This option downloads all data exactly as it is stored in the workbook. It does not apply any filters, sorting, column arrangements, or visibility settings from your current view. Downloading from a View (Excel or CSV): This option downloads the data with all current settings applied, including: Filters Sorting preferences Column visibility Column order

To download raw CSV for workbooks, do the following: On the Home page, from the left navigation panel, click Workspace, and from the list of workspaces, open the workspace where the workbook that you want to edit is located. Click the Workbook tab and select the required workbook. Click the Settings button on the top and select Download Raw CSV. The raw CSV is downloaded to your local system.

To download raw Excel for workbook, do the following: On the Home page, from the left navigation panel, click Workspace, and from the list of workspaces, open the workspace where the workbook that you want to edit is located. Click the Workbook tab and select the required workbook. Click the Settings button on the top and select Download Raw Excel. The raw Excel file is downloaded to your local system.

You can create email campaigns from Workbooks by selecting a view (master or filtered) and a recipient column (email or user). The view filters the recipients, sending the email only to a subset of members in the email or user column, rather than all of them. The email content can be personalized using variables corresponding to columns in the selected view. Moreover, you can preview the email and also send a test email to the users in your workspace. To create an email campaign do the following: Go to Workspaces and select a workbook. From the upper right side, click Actions and select Send Email Campaign. In the Create Email Campaign box, do the following: Select or create an email campaign: You can either select from the list of saved email campaigns or click Create New Campaign to create a new email campaign. Provide a name for the campaign: If you have selected the Create Newe Campaign option, provide a name for the campaign. This will help you track the campaign and also identify the email campaign in the Actions Library. Select receipients: In the Select Recipient box. You can choose either a user column or an email column as the recipient source. [Note] Only a column type of Email or User will be listed in the Select Receipient drop-down menu. If a user column is selected and it contains multiple users in a single cell, each user will receive the email individually. Select a view. This can be the master view or a filtered view. In the Select Recipient box. You can choose either a user column or an email column as the recipient source. If a user column is selected and it contains multiple users in a single cell, each user will receive the email individually. In the Draft Email box, you can create the email with the email subject and matter. Click Preview button to get a quick preview of the email. Click Send Test button to send a test email to yourself. DataGOL recommends sending a test email to yourself first. The test email will include a preview banner (attach image) to help you verify the content before sending it to others. Click Continue to Compose. In the Create Email Campaign box, type the email subject and body. You can dynamically include values from your workbook by referencing column names using the column_name notation. This ensures that personalized data from your workbook is seamlessly inserted into the email. You can also preview or send a test email. Click Review Campaign to validate the details of the email. The Email preview page is displayed. From here too, you can click the button to send a test email to your email address. Select the I confirm I want to send this campaign option and then click Send Campaign. The emails are sent to the intended recipients. [Limitations] There's a limit of 250 emails that can be sent at a time. Certain column types such as attachments and link are currently excluded from variable selection. Currently, email templates are not supported, so each email must be composed individually. We are working on adding this enhancement in the future. Attachments and link/join columns are also not supported Emails are not tracked currently. We are working on adding email tracking to prevent duplicate sends in a future update.

You can autosave and reuse an entire email campaign configuration. When you create a new campaign, the system saves all essential settings, including the template, message content, subject line, and the criteria used for selecting recipient columns, provided you have assigned a unique name for the email campaign. To reuse this saved configuration, you simply select the existing Email Campaign Name from the list. This action instantly loads all the previous details. This functionality promotes consistency across communications and significantly reduces the manual effort involved in setting up subsequent, similar email sends. To reuse an email campaign, do the following:

Enabling delete protection is highly recommended if your workbook is used in embedded analytics or as an API by another service. This ensures that critical data and configurations remain intact and prevents accidental or unauthorized deletions. info Enabling delete protection is highly recommended for workbooks utilized in embedded analytics, third-party integrations, or consumed via APIs. This protection ensures critical data and configurations remain secure and prevents accidental or unauthorized deletions. Delete protection can only be set by workbook owners and creators. A workbook that is delete-protected cannot be deleted. Additionally, users will be unable to delete an entire workspace if it contains even a single delete-protected workbook. This safeguard is particularly crucial for third-party integrations to ensure stability and prevent unintended disruptions to external dashboards or services relying on these resources. On the Home page, from the left navigation panel, click Workspace, and from the list of workspaces, open the workspace where the workbook that you want to edit is located. Click the Workbook tab and select the required workbook. Click the Settings button on the top and select Set Delete Protection. In the Delete Protection Settings box, select the Enable checkbox. Click Save. info The workspace in which there are workbooks with delete protection cannot be deleted. To delete such a workspace, you must remove the delete protection status for the workbooks.

Data extraction is the process of identifying and pulling specific pieces of information from unstructured documents. Imagine you have a pile of resumes, invoices, or shipping documents. Instead of manually sifting through each one to find the candidate's name, the invoice number, or the delivery address, data extraction automates this process. It helps you convert chaotic, unorganized data into structured, actionable information that can be easily analyzed and used. DataGOL uses AI to help you generate columns for your workbook output from the extracted data. You can guide the AI by providing clear and specific prompts and instructions for each column you want to extract. The more precise you are with your instructions to the AI, the more accurate data gets extracted. You also have the flexibility to create and save multiple extraction configurations for the same set of documents.
